objects.description: Function pointer type for a user_data cleanup callback. When provided to APIs that accept a user_data pointer, this callback can be invoked to free or finalize that user data. Calling convention follows API_CALL (cdecl on MSVC, default elsewhere).

Configuration record for initializing the ZLMediaKit C API environment via mk_env_init/mk_env_init2. Controls threading, logging, config source, and SSL certificate parameters. All fields must be set by the caller before use; string pointers may be NULL as documented. Lifetimes of pointed-to strings must outlive the call to mk_env_init; ownership is not transferred.

Callback table type holding function pointers for all ZLMediaKit C API event hooks defined in this header. Users fill desired callbacks and pass an instance to mk_events_listen to subscribe/unsubscribe to events. Many parameter types referenced here (e.g., mk_media_info, mk_sock_info) are defined in other headers and are not defined here. Unknown ownership/lifetime details for those external types; this struct itself is a POD container of callbacks.
Opaque handle to a RecordInfo object exposed by the C API. Represents metadata for a recording (start time, duration, file path/name, size, etc.). Concrete struct contents are hidden in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_parser_header_cb)(void *user_data, const char *key, const char *val);
objects.description: Function pointer type for iterating HTTP headers parsed by a Parser. Called with user_data and each header key/value pair.
Opaque handle to an HTTP parser object. Provides accessors for method, URL, query parameters, headers, tail/protocol string, and body, plus a foreach to iterate headers.
Opaque handle representing parsed media URL/info components (schema, vhost, app, stream, host, port, params).
Function pointer type invoked when a MediaSource search operation finds a media source.

Opaque handle to a MediaSource (live/on-demand stream) within ZLMediaKit. Exposes metadata (schema, vhost, app, stream), reader counts, tracks, origin info, lifecycle controls (close/seek/set speed), RTP sending controls, and discovery/iteration.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_media_source_send_rtp_result)(void *user_data, uint16_t local_port, int err, const char *msg);
objects.description: Function pointer type for asynchronous result notifications of starting RTP push from a MediaSource. Supplies local RTP port and error code/message.
Opaque handle to an HTTP body object. Can be constructed from string, buffer, file, or multipart form. Must be released with mk_http_body_release when no longer used.

Opaque handle used by HttpSession to send an HTTP response. Supports sending with a mk_http_body, with a string body, or directly from a file; can be cloned for async cross-thread invocation and the clone must be released with mk_http_response_invoker_clone_release.
Opaque handle used to conclude an HTTP access-path authorization check. Allows specifying error message, permitted root path, and cookie lifetime; can be cloned for async use and released.
Opaque handle to answer RtspSession::onGetRealm callback by providing the authentication realm string (or null/empty to disable auth). Cloneable for async use.
Opaque handle to answer RtspSession::onAuth by supplying a password (plain or MD5) with an encrypted flag. Cloneable for async use.

Opaque handle to complete Broadcast publish authorization, returning error message (null/empty on success) and enabling options such as HLS/MP4 or passing an mk_ini option set. Cloneable for async use.
Opaque handle to complete a generic Broadcast authorization by returning an error message (null/empty on success). Cloneable for async use.
Opaque handle for a WebRTC transport/data channel context. Used to send SCTP data channel messages with given stream id and PPID.

Opaque handle to a media frame object managed by the ZLMediaKit C API. Represents a single audio/video frame with codec, timestamps, flags, and payload accessible via API functions. Reference-counted; use mk_frame_ref/mk_frame_unref to manage lifetime. Internal structure is not exposed here.

Callback function pointer type invoked to release a user-supplied data buffer associated with a frame. If provided to mk_frame_create/mk_frame_create2, it will be called when the frame no longer needs the data.
Opaque handle to a buffer object used by frame merger callbacks to deliver merged frame data. The concrete structure is not defined here.
Opaque handle for a frame merger that aggregates input frames into combined buffers according to a chosen start-code/length-prefix mode (AnnexB or avcC).

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_frame_merger)(void *user_data, uint64_t dts, uint64_t pts, mk_buffer buffer, int have_key_frame);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type used by the frame merger to emit merged data along with timing and keyframe presence.
Opaque handle to an MPEG PS/TS muxer that packages input frames into PS or TS output via a user callback. Tracks must be initialized before feeding frames.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_mpeg_muxer_frame)(void *user_data, mk_mpeg_muxer muxer, const char *frame, size_t size, uint64_t timestamp, int key_pos);
objects.description: Callback function pointer type for receiving muxed PS/TS output data chunks with timestamp and keyframe info.
Opaque handle to a PS decoder that parses MPEG-PS streams and emits stream and frame callbacks. Only available when ENABLE_RTPPROXY is defined.

Opaque handle to an H.264/H.265 frame-splitter instance. The underlying struct mk_h264_splitter_t is not defined in this header, indicating a private implementation. Use mk_h264_splitter_create/mk_h264_splitter_create2 to construct, mk_h264_splitter_release to destroy, and mk_h264_splitter_input_data to feed bytestream data for frame extraction. Details of internal fields and lifetime semantics beyond these functions are not exposed here.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_h264_splitter_frame)(void *user_data, mk_h264_splitter splitter, const char *frame, int size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving output frames from the H.264/H.265 splitter. The callback is invoked with the user_data supplied at creation time, the splitter handle, a pointer to the frame buffer, and its size in bytes. Callbacks are set at construction via mk_h264_splitter_create/create2. Threading and buffer lifetime semantics are not specified here.

Opaque handle to an HTTP/HTTPS downloader object. The concrete struct mk_http_downloader_t is not defined in this header; users manage the handle via the provided API to create, start downloads to a file path, and release it.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_download_complete)(void *user_data, int code, const char *err_msg, const char *file_path);
objects.description: Function pointer type for download completion callbacks. Invoked when an HTTP/HTTPS download finishes or fails. code==0 indicates success; err_msg contains an error description on failure; file_path is the path where the file was saved.

Opaque handle to an HTTP requester object that can perform HTTP/HTTPS requests with configurable method, headers, and body, and then expose response status, headers, and body. The underlying struct is intentionally hidden and managed via the API.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_http_requester_complete)(void *user_data, int code, const char *err_msg);
objects.description: Function pointer type for HTTP requester completion callbacks. Triggered when a request completes or fails. code==0 indicates a complete HTTP session with a received response; err_msg contains an error description on failure. The associated mk_http_requester is expected to be reachable via user_data.

Opaque handle type for a media source instance in ZLMediaKit. This is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct, used as the primary context for creating, configuring, feeding frames to, and controlling a media source. The actual struct layout is hidden from the API consumer.

Function-pointer callback type invoked when an associated MediaSource is requested to close. Implementations should release resources and call mk_media_release on the corresponding mk_media within this callback to honor the close request.
Function-pointer callback type for handling client seek requests. Return 1 to accept and handle the seek to the specified timestamp in milliseconds, or 0 to ignore.

objects.definition: typedef int(API_CALL* on_mk_media_pause)(void* user_data, int pause);
objects.description: Function-pointer callback type for handling pause/resume requests from clients. The pause parameter is 1 for pause and 0 for resume. Return value semantics are not explicitly documented but typically 1 means handled.

objects.definition: typedef int(API_CALL* on_mk_media_speed)(void* user_data, float speed);
objects.description: Function-pointer callback type for handling playback speed change requests (e.g., 0.5, 1.0, 2.0). Return value semantics mirror other control callbacks; typically return 1 if handled.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_media_source_regist)(void *user_data, mk_media_source sender, int regist);
objects.description: Function-pointer callback type fired when a MediaSource is registered (regist=1) or unregistered (regist=0) with the framework. The sender is an mk_media_source handle (defined elsewhere).

Alias typedef of the function-pointer type used for reporting the result of starting RTP streaming. The underlying base type on_mk_media_source_send_rtp_result is defined in another header. This header only introduces an alias name for convenience when working with mk_media APIs.

Opaque handle type for a media player instance supporting RTMP/RTMPS and RTSP/RTSPS playback. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct mk_player_t, exposing mk_player as the public handle. The underlying struct definition is not provided in this header, making this an opaque type managed via the mk_player_* API.

objects.definition:
typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_play_event)(void *user_data, int err_code, const char *err_msg, mk_track tracks[],
                                         int track_count);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks invoked on playback result (success/failure) or abnormal interruption. The callback receives a user-supplied pointer, an error code, an error message, and an array of mk_track along with its count. The mk_track type is referenced from mk_track.h and is not defined here.

Opaque handle type for a proxy media player managed by the ZLMediaKit C API. It represents a player instance that can pull a remote stream (e.g., RTSP/RTMP) and optionally restream/proxy it with HLS/MP4 generation and retry behavior. The underlying struct is not defined in this header and is intended to be used as an opaque pointer.

objects.definition:
typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_proxy_player_cb)(void *user_data, int err, const char *what, int sys_err);
#define on_mk_proxy_player_close on_mk_proxy_player_cb
objects.description: Function pointer type for proxy player event callbacks, used for MediaSource.close notifications and first-play result events. The callback receives user_data, an error code, a descriptive message string, and a system error code. The macro on_mk_proxy_player_close is a compatibility alias of this type.

Opaque handle to a pusher object used to publish a registered MediaSource to rtsp[s]/rtmp[s] destinations. The underlying struct mk_pusher_t is intentionally not exposed here; treat this as a managed handle created by mk_pusher_create/mk_pusher_create_src and released with mk_pusher_release.

Function pointer type for pusher result/shutdown callbacks. Called with user_data, an error code (0 means success), and an error message. Register it via mk_pusher_set_on_result[2] and mk_pusher_set_on_shutdown[2].

Opaque handle type for an FLV recorder instance. The underlying struct mk_flv_recorder_t is forward-declared and not defined in this header, indicating it is managed by the library and should be treated as an opaque pointer.
Opaque or external configuration handle referenced for loading MP4 files. This type is not defined in this header; it is likely declared in mk_common.h or mk_util.h. Details are unknown here.

Opaque handle to a GB28181 RTP server instance managed by the ZLMediaKit C API. The underlying struct is not exposed here; use the provided API functions to create, connect (TCP active mode), configure, and release the server. Ownership and lifecycle are managed by the caller via the create/release functions.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_rtp_server_connected)(void *user_data, int err, const char *what, int sys_err);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the callback invoked when attempting to connect to a remote server in TCP active mode for an RTP server. Parameters provide user data, high-level error code, message text, and system error code.
Function pointer type for a callback triggered when the GB28181 RTP server times out waiting for an incoming RTP stream (detach event). Receives the user-provided context pointer.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_rtp_get_info)(int exist, const char *peer_ip, uint16_t peer_port, const char *local_ip, uint16_t local_port, const char *identifier);
objects.description: Function pointer type for asynchronously receiving RTP push information for an app/stream, including whether it exists, peer/local IP and ports, and an identifier string.

Opaque handle to a reference-counted buffer used for passing data to/from TCP APIs. Lifetime is managed via mk_buffer_ref/mk_buffer_unref and by ownership transfer in send APIs. Underlying storage may be caller-owned if provided with a free callback.
Function pointer type invoked to free user-provided buffer memory when a mk_buffer releases ownership.
Opaque socket information handle exposing peer/local IP and port for sessions/clients.
Opaque TCP session handle representing a server-side connection accepted by the custom TCP server.
Opaque strong-reference handle that keeps the associated mk_tcp_session alive independently of thread/ownership context.
Callback vtable for server-side TCP sessions: creation, data, periodic manager, and disconnect notifications.
Enumeration of TCP transport types: plain TCP, SSL/TLS, WebSocket, and secure WebSocket.
Opaque TCP client handle used to initiate and manage outbound connections.
Callback vtable for client-side TCP: connect result, disconnect, inbound data, and periodic manager timer.

Opaque handle to an event thread used by ZLMediaKit for timers and network I/O. Represents threads from the main event-thread pool or background work pool. Actual structure is not defined in this header.
Opaque handle to a thread pool that manages multiple event threads with configurable size and priority.

Function-pointer type for asynchronous/synchronous callbacks executed on a specified event thread. The callback receives a user_data pointer; lifetime management may be provided via paired APIs that accept an on_user_data_free, which is declared elsewhere.
Opaque handle to a repeating or one-shot timer associated with an event thread. Timer callbacks run on the owning thread.
Function-pointer type for timer callbacks. Return value is the next delay in milliseconds; returning 0 stops repetition.
Opaque handle to a semaphore primitive for cross-thread synchronization (post/wait).

Opaque handle to an audio/video track object managed by the ZLMediaKit C API. It is a reference-counted object; create via mk_track_create and manage lifetime with mk_track_ref/mk_track_unref. The underlying struct mk_track_t is not defined in this header (opaque).

Function pointer type for frame output callbacks invoked by a track to deliver frames to the user. The callback receives the user_data pointer supplied during registration and a mk_frame representing the produced frame.

Union of codec parameter sets used when creating a track. For video, specify width/height/fps. For audio, specify channels/sample_rate. Which member is used depends on the codec_id passed to mk_track_create.
Opaque handle to a decoder instance owned and managed by this API. Actual struct is hidden; use provided constructor/destructor and methods.
Opaque handle to a decoded pixel frame wrapper around FFmpeg AVFrame, with ref-count semantics managed via mk_frame_pix_ref/unref.
Opaque handle to an FFmpeg SwsContext wrapper for pixel format/size conversion.
Forward declaration of FFmpeg AVFrame. Not defined here; provided for interop. Allocation/ownership not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of FFmpeg AVCodecContext used for accessing the underlying decoder context.
Function pointer type for decode output callbacks. Called with user_data and an mk_frame_pix representing the decoded frame.

Opaque handle to an INI configuration object used by the ZLMediaKit C API. The underlying struct mk_ini_t is not defined in this header, so the type is used as a handle for creating, loading, querying, modifying, and releasing INI configurations via the provided API functions.

Function-pointer callback type invoked by mk_get_statistic to deliver collected statistics. The callback receives the user_data pointer provided to mk_get_statistic and an mk_ini handle containing the statistics.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_webrtc_get_answer_sdp)(void *user_data, const char *answer, const char *err);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving a generated WebRTC answer SDP or an error. The callback is invoked with the user_data provided to the initiating API, the resulting answer string, and an error string if generation failed.
Function pointer type for receiving WebRTC proxy player information as a JSON string or an error message.

objects.definition: typedef void(API_CALL *on_mk_webrtc_room_keeper_info_cb)(void *user_data, const char *room_key, const char *err);
objects.description: Function pointer type invoked on registration to or deregistration from the signaling server. Provides user_data, the assigned room_key, and an error string if applicable.
Function pointer type for receiving room-keeper listing data, likely in JSON format, when querying peer or server registration info.

This header is an umbrella aggregator for the ZLMediaKit C API. It does not itself define any custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes); it only includes other headers where those types are defined.

functions.name: mk_env_init
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_env_init(const mk_config *cfg);
functions.description: Initialize the ZLMediaKit runtime environment. Must be called before using any other APIs in this library. Accepts a configuration struct that controls threads, logging, configuration file handling, and TLS/SSL settings. Suitable for C/C++ callers that can populate mk_config.
requirements: Must be called before invoking other library functions.
cfg points to a valid mk_config struct; field meanings follow the comments in mk_config.
cfg->log_level supports values 0~4.
cfg->log_mask is a bitmask composed of LOG_CONSOLE, LOG_FILE, LOG_CALLBACK, etc.
cfg->log_file_path may be NULL to disable logging to file.
cfg->log_file_days: set to 0 to disable log file; other range constraints are unknown.
cfg->ini_is_path indicates whether cfg->ini is file content or a path; cfg->ini may be NULL. If a path is provided and the file does not exist, default configuration will be exported to that file.
cfg->ssl_is_path indicates whether cfg->ssl is certificate content or a path; cfg->ssl may be NULL; cfg->ssl_pwd may be NULL.
Other value ranges (e.g., thread_num, log_mask specifics) are not explicitly constrained beyond the notes above.

functions.name: mk_stop_all_server
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_stop_all_server();
functions.description: Shut down all servers started by the library. Intended to be called during program shutdown (e.g., before exiting main).
requirements: Call when exiting the main function to close all servers.
No parameters; additional ordering or repeat-call constraints are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: mk_env_init2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_env_init2(int thread_num, int log_level, int log_mask, const char *log_file_path, int log_file_days, int ini_is_path, const char *ini, int ssl_is_path, const char *ssl, const char *ssl_pwd);
functions.description: Initialize the environment using basic-typed parameters for easier use from other languages. Equivalent in effect to mk_env_init with mk_config. Controls threads, logging, configuration file handling, and TLS/SSL settings.
requirements: Must be called before invoking other library functions.
thread_num: number of threads; exact valid range is not specified (unknown).
log_level: supports values 0~4.
log_mask: mask controlling log output; combine LOG_CONSOLE, LOG_FILE, LOG_CALLBACK, etc.; exact composition rules beyond bitmask use are not specified.
log_file_path: set to NULL to disable logging to file.
log_file_days: set to 0 to disable log file; other range constraints are not specified (unknown).
ini_is_path: nonzero indicates ini is a file path; zero indicates content; ini may be NULL. If a path is provided and the file does not exist, default configuration will be exported to that file.
ssl_is_path: nonzero indicates ssl is a file path; zero indicates certificate content; ssl may be NULL; ssl_pwd may be NULL.

functions.name: mk_set_log
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_log(int file_max_size, int file_max_count);
functions.description: Configure log file rotation: set the maximum size (in MB) for each log file slice and the maximum number of slices to retain.
requirements: file_max_size: per-file slice size in MB; specific valid range is not documented (unknown).
file_max_count: number of slice files; specific valid range is not documented (unknown).
Effect on existing logging configuration and whether it must be called before/after mk_env_init is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: mk_set_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_option(const char *key, const char *val);
functions.description: Deprecated: set a configuration option by key/value. Prefer mk_ini_set_option. Intended to adjust configuration at runtime.
requirements: Function is deprecated; callers should use mk_ini_set_option instead when available.
key: configuration item name; exact allowed keys and whether NULL is permitted are not documented (unknown).
val: configuration item value; valid formats and whether NULL is permitted are not documented (unknown).
Error reporting behavior is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: mk_get_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char * API_CALL mk_get_option(const char *key);
functions.description: Deprecated: retrieve the value of a configuration option by key. Prefer mk_ini_get_option. Returns a pointer to a string representing the value.
requirements: Function is deprecated; callers should use mk_ini_get_option instead when available.
key: configuration item name; valid keys and NULL handling are not documented (unknown).
Return value lifetime/ownership and whether NULL may be returned on failure or missing key are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: mk_http_server_start
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint16_t API_CALL mk_http_server_start(uint16_t port, int ssl);
functions.description: Start an HTTP or HTTPS server. Returns the listening port on success, or 0 on failure. For convenience, a port of 0 lets the library pick a free port. ssl selects HTTP (0) or HTTPS (nonzero).
requirements: port: recommended 80; passing 0 allows the library to randomly allocate a free port.
ssl: whether this is an SSL server; treated as boolean (0 = non-SSL, nonzero = SSL) per documentation wording; exact accepted values beyond 0/nonzero are not specified.
Must be called after environment initialization (implied typical flow; explicit requirement not stated beyond general usage).

functions.name: mk_events_listen
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_events_listen(const mk_events *events);
functions.description: Registers or unregisters a set of event callbacks with ZLMediaKit. Pass a pointer to an mk_events structure to start or update the event listeners; pass NULL to cancel listening. The mk_events structure is copied internally, so the caller does not need to keep the original structure alive after the call. Typical usage: fill an mk_events instance with desired callback function pointers (leave unused ones NULL) and call mk_events_listen(&ev). Call mk_events_listen(NULL) to remove previously registered listeners.
requirements: events may be NULL to cancel listening.
If events is non-NULL, it must point to a valid mk_events struct whose fields match the declared callback signatures.
Only callbacks with the exact required signatures and calling convention (API_CALL) should be assigned; unused callbacks can be set to NULL.
The mk_events struct is copied internally; the pointer need not remain valid after the function returns.

functions.name: mk_record_info_get_start_time
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_record_info_get_start_time(const mk_record_info ctx);
functions.description: Returns the GMT start time (in seconds) of the recording represented by the mk_record_info handle. Use to query when a recording started.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_record_info obtained from the SDK.
The returned value is a timestamp in seconds since the epoch (per comment).
The lifetime/ownership of ctx is managed elsewhere; must remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: mk_frame_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame API_CALL mk_frame_create(int codec_id, uint64_t dts, uint64_t pts, const char *data, size_t size, on_mk_frame_data_release cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Creates a new reference-counted frame object with the specified codec, timestamps, and payload. If cb is null, the implementation copies data internally; otherwise it is expected to take ownership of data and later invoke cb(user_data, data_ptr) to release it. Use mk_frame_unref to drop your reference when done; use mk_frame_ref to add an extra reference.
requirements: codec_id must be one of the MKCodecXXX constants.
data must point to a single frame buffer of length size.
If cb is null, data may be transient; the function copies it internally.
If cb is non-null, the caller must ensure data remains valid until the library later invokes cb to release it.
user_data is opaque and passed back to cb.
Returned mk_frame must be released with mk_frame_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_frame_create2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame API_CALL mk_frame_create2(int codec_id, uint64_t dts, uint64_t pts, const char *data, size_t size, on_mk_frame_data_release cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Creates a new frame object like mk_frame_create, additionally accepting a user_data_free callback to release user_data when the frame is finalized. Intended for cases where ownership of both data and its associated context is transferred to the frame.
requirements: Same requirements as mk_frame_create for codec_id, data, size, and cb.
If user_data_free is provided, the implementation may call it to free user_data when appropriate; user_data must be valid until that time.
Returned mk_frame must be released with mk_frame_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_frame_unref
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_unref(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the frame object and releases it when the count reaches zero. After the final unref, the frame and any associated buffers become invalid.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame obtained from mk_frame_create/mk_frame_create2 or mk_frame_ref.
Do not use frame after its reference count reaches zero (i.e., after the final mk_frame_unref).
Thread-safety of unref is unknown; follow library threading model if any.

functions.name: mk_frame_ref
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame API_CALL mk_frame_ref(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the given frame and returns a new reference handle to the same underlying object.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.
Each successful call adds a reference that must later be released with mk_frame_unref.

functions.name: mk_frame_codec_id
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_frame_codec_id(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns the codec identifier of the frame. Values correspond to MKCodecXXX constants.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_codec_name
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char* API_CALL mk_frame_codec_name(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable codec name for the frame’s codec.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.
Returned pointer lifetime and ownership are unspecified; treat as read-only and do not free.

functions.name: mk_frame_is_video
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_frame_is_video(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Indicates whether the frame is a video frame (non-zero) or not (zero).
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_data
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char* API_CALL mk_frame_get_data(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the frame payload data.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.
Pointer remains valid while the frame reference is alive; do not free it.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_data_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT size_t API_CALL mk_frame_get_data_size(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the frame payload.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_data_prefix_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT size_t API_CALL mk_frame_get_data_prefix_size(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of any codec-specific start-code/prefix in the payload (e.g., 4 for Annex-B 0x00 00 00 01).
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_dts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_frame_get_dts(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns the decoding timestamp (milliseconds) of the frame.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_pts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_frame_get_pts(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns the presentation/display timestamp (milliseconds) of the frame.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_get_flags
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint32_t API_CALL mk_frame_get_flags(mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Returns bitwise flags describing the frame. See MK_FRAME_FLAG_* defines (e.g., keyframe, config frame, drop-able, not-decode-able).
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame.

functions.name: mk_frame_merger_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame_merger API_CALL mk_frame_merger_create(int type);
functions.description: Creates a frame merger for aggregating frames/NAL units into larger buffers. type selects the start-code/header format: 0=none, 1=AnnexB (0x00 00 00 01), 2=mp4 NAL size (avcC).
requirements: type must be 0, 1, or 2 as documented.
Returned mk_frame_merger must later be released with mk_frame_merger_release.

functions.name: mk_frame_merger_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_merger_release(mk_frame_merger ctx);
functions.description: Destroys and frees a frame merger created by mk_frame_merger_create.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_frame_merger created by mk_frame_merger_create.
Do not use ctx after release.

functions.name: mk_frame_merger_clear
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_merger_clear(mk_frame_merger ctx);
functions.description: Clears internal buffers of the merger to allow reuse without reallocating.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_frame_merger.

functions.name: mk_frame_merger_input
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_merger_input(mk_frame_merger ctx, mk_frame frame, on_mk_frame_merger cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Feeds a frame into the merger. The merger may invoke cb with merged output buffer(s), their timestamps, and whether a key frame is included.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_frame_merger.
frame must be a valid mk_frame.
cb must be a valid function pointer; the merger relies on it for output.
user_data is opaque and passed to cb.
The callback may be invoked synchronously during the call; callers must be prepared for reentrancy if applicable.

functions.name: mk_frame_merger_flush
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_merger_flush(mk_frame_merger ctx);
functions.description: Forces flushing of any buffered data in the merger and triggers callbacks for remaining merged output. The docs require that mk_frame_merger_input has been called before and that callback parameters are valid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_frame_merger.
Before calling, ensure mk_frame_merger_input was called at least once and that the callback parameters supplied there remain valid.

functions.name: mk_mpeg_muxer_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_mpeg_muxer API_CALL mk_mpeg_muxer_create(on_mk_mpeg_muxer_frame cb, void *user_data, int is_ps);
functions.description: Creates an MPEG-PS/TS muxer and registers an output callback to receive packetized data. Set is_ps non-zero for PS, zero for TS.
requirements: cb must be a valid function pointer; it is used to deliver muxed output.
user_data is opaque and passed to cb.
is_ps selects the container: non-zero for PS, zero for TS.
Returned mk_mpeg_muxer must be released with mk_mpeg_muxer_release.

functions.name: mk_mpeg_muxer_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_mpeg_muxer_release(mk_mpeg_muxer ctx);
functions.description: Destroys the MPEG muxer created by mk_mpeg_muxer_create.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_mpeg_muxer.
Do not use ctx after release.

functions.name: mk_mpeg_muxer_init_track
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_mpeg_muxer_init_track(mk_mpeg_muxer ctx, void* track);
functions.description: Adds an audio/video track to the muxer (e.g., a codec/track descriptor). Typically called once per track before starting to mux frames.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_mpeg_muxer.
track must be a valid mk_track-like object as required by the library (exact type not specified in this header).

functions.name: mk_mpeg_muxer_init_complete
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_mpeg_muxer_init_complete(mk_mpeg_muxer ctx);
functions.description: Signals that track initialization is complete. For single-track streams, calling this avoids an extra ~3s wait before output begins.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_mpeg_muxer.
Should be called after all intended tracks have been added via mk_mpeg_muxer_init_track if you want to shorten startup latency for single-track streams.

functions.name: mk_mpeg_muxer_input_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_mpeg_muxer_input_frame(mk_mpeg_muxer ctx, mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Inputs a frame to the muxer for packetization. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_mpeg_muxer.
frame must be a valid mk_frame matching one of the initialized tracks’ formats.
Return value must be checked by the caller to handle failures.

functions.name: mk_ps_decoder_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_ps_decoder API_CALL mk_ps_decoder_create(on_mk_ps_decoder_stream scb, on_mk_ps_decoder_frame dcb, void * user_data);
functions.description: Creates a PS (Program Stream) parser/decoder. dcb is mandatory for receiving parsed frames. scb is optional and can be used to receive stream/track discovery events. Availability depends on the library being built with ENABLE_RTPPROXY.

functions.name: mk_ps_decoder_release

data must point to a buffer of PS data of length bytes; bytes may be zero only if the implementation supports it (unspecified).
Only available when built with ENABLE_RTPPROXY.

functions.name: mk_h264_splitter_create
functions.signature: mk_h264_splitter mk_h264_splitter_create(on_mk_h264_splitter_frame cb, void *user_data, int is_h265);
functions.description: Create a frame splitter that parses an H.264 or H.265 elementary stream fed via mk_h264_splitter_input_data and emits complete frames through the provided callback. Use this to segment raw bytestream data into frames. The is_h265 flag selects whether the input stream is H.265 (non-zero) or H.264 (zero). Details of threading and callback timing are not documented.
requirements: cb is a function of type on_mk_h264_splitter_frame; behavior if cb is NULL is not documented.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback unchanged.
is_h265 acts as a boolean selector: 0 for H.264, non-zero for H.265 (inferred from parameter name and comments).
The returned mk_h264_splitter must be released with mk_h264_splitter_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_h264_splitter_create2
functions.signature: mk_h264_splitter mk_h264_splitter_create2(on_mk_h264_splitter_frame cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free, int is_h265);
functions.description: Create a frame splitter for H.264/H.265 like mk_h264_splitter_create, but also supply a user_data_free callback that will be used to free or finalize user_data when the splitter is destroyed. Use this when user_data requires custom cleanup. The is_h265 flag selects H.265 (non-zero) vs H.264 (zero).
requirements: cb is a function of type on_mk_h264_splitter_frame; behavior if cb is NULL is not documented.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback unchanged.
user_data_free is a function of type on_user_data_free intended to clean up user_data; it may be called during object destruction (timing details are not documented; inference based on naming).
is_h265 acts as a boolean selector: 0 for H.264, non-zero for H.265 (inferred from parameter name and comments).
The returned mk_h264_splitter must be released with mk_h264_splitter_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_h264_splitter_release
functions.signature: void mk_h264_splitter_release(mk_h264_splitter ctx);
functions.description: Destroy and free a splitter previously created by mk_h264_splitter_create or mk_h264_splitter_create2. After this call, the splitter and any associated resources are invalid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_h264_splitter returned by mk_h264_splitter_create or mk_h264_splitter_create2.
Do not use ctx after this call (no further calls into the splitter).
Do not call this function more than once for the same ctx (no double-free).

functions.name: mk_h264_splitter_input_data
functions.signature: void mk_h264_splitter_input_data(mk_h264_splitter ctx, const char *data, int size);
functions.description: Feed raw H.264/H.265 bytestream data into the splitter for parsing. The splitter may emit zero or more frames via the registered callback as it parses the input chunk. Intended to be called repeatedly as new stream data arrives.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_h264_splitter created by mk_h264_splitter_create or mk_h264_splitter_create2 and not yet released.
data must point to a readable buffer containing h264/h265 data of at least size bytes.
size must be non-negative; if zero, no data is processed; negative values are invalid (inferred from type and common API practice).
The format of data should match the is_h265 mode selected at creation (inferred from API).

functions.name: mk_http_downloader_create

functions.name: mk_http_downloader_release

functions.name: mk_http_downloader_start

file must be a valid file save path accessible to the process.

functions.name: mk_http_downloader_start2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_http_downloader_start2(mk_http_downloader ctx, const char *url, const char *file, on_mk_download_complete cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Start an HTTP/HTTPS download with an optional user_data destructor. Behaves like mk_http_downloader_start but also accepts a callback to free user_data when appropriate.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_http_downloader.
url must be an http or https URL.
file must be a valid file save path accessible to the process.
If user_data_free is provided, it must be callable for cleaning up user_data.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_http_requester API_CALL mk_http_requester_create();
functions.description: Create an HttpRequester object used to perform generic HTTP/HTTPS requests and access their responses.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_clear

functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_http_requester_set_method(mk_http_requester ctx, const char *method);

functions.name: mk_http_requester_set_header
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_http_requester_set_header(mk_http_requester ctx, const char *header[]);

functions.name: mk_http_requester_set_body
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_http_requester_set_body(mk_http_requester ctx, mk_http_body body);
functions.description: Set the HTTP message body using an mk_http_body (e.g., created by mk_http_body_from_string). Caller should release the body with mk_http_body_release after use.
requirements: body must be an mk_http_body object created via provided constructors such as mk_http_body_from_string.

ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_get_response_status
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char* API_CALL mk_http_requester_get_response_status(mk_http_requester ctx);
functions.description: Get the HTTP response status text after a response is received (e.g., "200 OK").

ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_get_response_header
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char* API_CALL mk_http_requester_get_response_header(mk_http_requester ctx, const char *key);

requirements: Call only after the HTTP response has been received (i.e., completion callback reported code == 0).
ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char* API_CALL mk_http_requester_get_response_body(mk_http_requester ctx, size_t *length);
functions.description: Get a pointer to the response body and optionally its length after a response is received.
requirements: Call only after the HTTP response has been received (i.e., completion callback reported code == 0).

ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

requirements: Call only after the HTTP response has been received (i.e., completion callback reported code == 0).
ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_set_cb2

functions.description: Set the completion callback with an optional user_data destructor for cleanup after completion.
requirements: cb must not be NULL (cannot be empty).
If user_data_free is provided, it must be callable for cleaning up user_data.
ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.

functions.name: mk_http_requester_start
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_http_requester_start(mk_http_requester ctx, const char *url, float timeout_second);
functions.description: Start an HTTP/HTTPS request to the given URL with a maximum timeout. On completion, the set callback is invoked; then access response data via the get_response APIs.
requirements: url must be an http or https URL.
timeout_second specifies the maximum timeout in seconds.
ctx must be a valid mk_http_requester.
