Returned mk_media must be released with mk_media_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_media_create2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_media API_CALL mk_media_create2(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, float duration, mk_ini option);
functions.description: Create a media source with ProtocolOption-related configuration provided via mk_ini. duration is in seconds (0 for live). Returns an mk_media handle.
requirements: vhost, app, stream must be valid null-terminated strings.
duration is in seconds; use 0 for live streams.
option must be a valid mk_ini (ProtocolOption config). Exact keys/values are not documented here (unknown).
Release the returned mk_media with mk_media_release when done.

functions.name: mk_media_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_release(mk_media ctx);
functions.description: Destroy and release a media source created by mk_media_create/mk_media_create2. Should also be invoked from the MediaSource.close() callback to actually close the source and free resources.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle previously created by mk_media_create or mk_media_create2.
After calling, ctx becomes invalid and must not be used again.
If called from on_mk_media_close, ensure any associated resources are freed as well.

functions.name: mk_media_init_track
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_init_track(mk_media ctx, mk_track track);
functions.description: Add an audio or video track to the media source using a mk_track object. Preferred API for adding tracks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
track must be a valid mk_track representing an initialized audio or video track.
Should be called before sending frames for that track.
If the stream is single-track and no more tracks will be added, call mk_media_init_complete to avoid an extra 3s wait.

functions.name: mk_media_init_video
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_init_video(mk_media ctx, int codec_id, int width, int height, float fps, int bit_rate);
functions.description: Deprecated-style API to add a video track directly by parameters (use mk_media_init_track instead). codec_id 0=H264, 1=H265. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
codec_id must be 0 (H264) or 1 (H265).
width, height, fps, bit_rate are meaningful only when encoding (per comments).
Call prior to submitting video frames.
Return value must be checked: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_init_audio
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_init_audio(mk_media ctx, int codec_id, int sample_rate, int channels, int sample_bit);
functions.description: Deprecated-style API to add an audio track by parameters (prefer mk_media_init_track). codec_id 2=AAC, 3=G711A, 4=G711U, 5=OPUS. sample_bit supports only 16. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
codec_id must be one of 2 (AAC), 3 (G711A), 4 (G711U), 5 (OPUS).
sample_rate must be a positive integer (exact supported rates unspecified; unknown).
channels must be a positive integer (typical 1 or 2; exact limits unknown).
sample_bit must be 16 (only supported value).
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_init_complete
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_init_complete(mk_media ctx);
functions.description: Signal that track initialization (h264/h265/aac) is complete. Especially useful for single-track streams to avoid an internal 3-second wait before the stream becomes available.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
Call after finishing adding all intended tracks, particularly for single-track streams.

functions.name: mk_media_input_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_frame(mk_media ctx, mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Submit a media frame (audio or video) to the media source. Preferred API for inputting encoded frames.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with corresponding tracks initialized.
frame must be a valid mk_frame corresponding to one of the added tracks and properly populated (codec-specific payload, dts/pts as required).
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure; callers should check the result.
Frames should match the codec/format of the initialized track.

functions.name: mk_media_input_h264
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_h264(mk_media ctx, const void *data, int len, uint64_t dts, uint64_t pts);
functions.description: Submit a single H.264 frame. Accepts NAL start codes of 00 00 01 or 00 00 00 01. Prefer mk_media_input_frame for new code. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with an H.264 video track initialized.
data must point to a complete single H.264 frame with start codes (00 00 01 or 00 00 00 01).
len must be the byte size of the frame and > 0.
dts is the decode timestamp in milliseconds.
pts is the presentation timestamp in milliseconds.
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_input_h265
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_h265(mk_media ctx, const void *data, int len, uint64_t dts, uint64_t pts);
functions.description: Submit a single H.265 frame. Accepts NAL start codes of 00 00 01 or 00 00 00 01. Prefer mk_media_input_frame for new code. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with an H.265 video track initialized.
data must point to a complete single H.265 frame with start codes (00 00 01 or 00 00 00 01).
len must be the byte size of the frame and > 0.
dts is the decode timestamp in milliseconds.
pts is the presentation timestamp in milliseconds.
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_input_yuv
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_input_yuv(mk_media ctx, const char *yuv[3], int linesize[3], uint64_t cts);
functions.description: Submit raw YUV420p video planes for encoding/processing. yuv points to three planes (Y, U, V) and linesize supplies their strides. cts is the capture timestamp in milliseconds.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle and configured to accept raw YUV input (typically after initializing a video track that expects raw input; exact encoder bindings unknown).
yuv must provide three valid plane pointers for Y, U, V in YUV420p layout.
linesize must contain three non-negative stride values corresponding to yuv planes.
cts is a timestamp in milliseconds.

functions.name: mk_media_input_aac
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_aac(mk_media ctx, const void *data, int len, uint64_t dts, void *adts);
functions.description: Submit a single AAC frame without ADTS header, with a separate 7-byte ADTS header provided via adts (can be null). Prefer mk_media_input_frame for new code. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with an AAC audio track initialized.
data must point to one AAC frame payload without ADTS header.
len must be the byte size of the AAC frame and > 0.
dts is the timestamp in milliseconds.
adts points to a 7-byte ADTS header or can be null if not needed/available.
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_input_pcm
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_pcm(mk_media ctx, void *data, int len, uint64_t pts);
functions.description: Submit a single PCM audio frame. Only effective when the library is built with ENABLE_FAAC. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with a compatible audio track initialized for PCM ingestion/encoding (details depend on build; unknown).
Library must be compiled with ENABLE_FAAC for this function to be effective.
data must point to PCM samples; format specifics (sample rate, channels, sample bit) must match the initialized audio track (unknown exact packing).
len must be the byte length of the PCM frame and > 0.
pts is a timestamp in milliseconds.
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_input_audio
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_input_audio(mk_media ctx, const void* data, int len, uint64_t dts);
functions.description: Submit a single OPUS/G711 audio frame. Prefer mk_media_input_frame for new code. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle with an OPUS or G711 audio track initialized.
data must point to one encoded audio frame for the corresponding codec.
len must be the byte length of the audio frame and > 0.
dts is the timestamp in milliseconds.
Check return value: 1=success, 0=failure.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_close
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_close(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_close cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when MediaSource.close() is requested on the associated source. Within the callback you should call mk_media_release and free other resources. If you do not call mk_media_release, MediaSource.close() will be ineffective.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to clear the callback, otherwise must be a valid function pointer taking user_data.
user_data must remain valid until the callback is cleared or the media is released.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_close2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_close2(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_close cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a close callback with an optional destructor for user_data. When the callback is cleared or media destroyed, user_data_free will be invoked to free user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to clear the callback; otherwise must be a valid function pointer.
user_data may be null; if non-null it must be valid until user_data_free is called.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_seek
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_seek(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_seek cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback for client seek requests. The callback receives the target timestamp in milliseconds and should return 1 to handle the seek or 0 to ignore.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable seek handling; otherwise must match on_mk_media_seek signature.
user_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the callback registration.
The callback should return 1 to indicate it will process the seek, 0 to ignore.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_seek2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_seek2(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_seek cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a seek callback with an optional destructor for user_data. The callback indicates whether the seek will be processed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable; otherwise must match on_mk_media_seek signature.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is invoked by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_pause
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_pause(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_pause cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback for client pause/resume requests. The callback receives pause=1 to pause and pause=0 to resume and returns an int (non-zero to accept, zero to ignore).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable pause handling; otherwise must match on_mk_media_pause signature.
user_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the callback registration.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_pause2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_pause2(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_pause cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a pause/resume callback with an optional destructor for user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable; otherwise must match on_mk_media_pause signature.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is invoked by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_speed
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_speed(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_speed cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback for client playback speed change requests (e.g., 0.5, 1.0, 2.0). The callback returns an int (non-zero to accept, zero to ignore).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable speed handling; otherwise must match on_mk_media_speed signature.
user_data must remain valid for the lifetime of the callback registration.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_speed2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_speed2(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_speed cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a speed-change callback with an optional destructor for user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to disable; otherwise must match on_mk_media_speed signature.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is invoked by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_total_reader_count
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_media_total_reader_count(mk_media ctx);
functions.description: Return the total number of viewers (readers) currently attached to this media source.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_regist
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_regist(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_source_regist cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback for MediaSource registration/unregistration events for this media. Callback provides the generated MediaSource object and a flag regist (1=registered, 0=unregistered).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to clear; otherwise must match on_mk_media_source_regist signature.
user_data must remain valid until the callback is cleared or media is released.

functions.name: mk_media_set_on_regist2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_set_on_regist2(mk_media ctx, on_mk_media_source_regist cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a registration/unregistration callback with an optional destructor for user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
cb may be null to clear; otherwise must match on_mk_media_source_regist signature.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is invoked by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_start_send_rtp
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_start_send_rtp(mk_media ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, const char *ssrc, int con_type, on_mk_media_send_rtp_result cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Start sending a PS-over-RTP stream for this media to the specified destination. Distinguishes multiple streams by SSRC. Thread-safe. Invokes callback on first success/failure (subsequent retries occur after initial success).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
dst_url must be a valid null-terminated hostname or IP string.
dst_port is the destination port.
ssrc must be a decimal string representing the RTP SSRC.
con_type must be one of: 0=tcp active, 1=udp active, 2=tcp passive, 3=udp passive.
cb may be null; if provided, must match on_mk_media_send_rtp_result signature.
user_data must remain valid until the operation completes or the callback is cleared.
This API is documented as thread-safe.

functions.name: mk_media_start_send_rtp2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_start_send_rtp2(mk_media ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, const char *ssrc, int con_type, on_mk_media_send_rtp_result cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Start sending PS-over-RTP with a callback and a user_data destructor. Thread-safe.
requirements: Same as mk_media_start_send_rtp for ctx, dst_url, dst_port, ssrc, con_type.
cb may be null; if provided, must match on_mk_media_send_rtp_result signature.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is called by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_start_send_rtp3
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_start_send_rtp3(mk_media ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, const char *ssrc, int con_type, mk_ini options, on_mk_media_send_rtp_result cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Start sending PS-over-RTP with additional options provided via mk_ini. Thread-safe. Invokes callback on start success/failure.
requirements: Same as mk_media_start_send_rtp for ctx, dst_url, dst_port, ssrc, con_type.
options must be a valid mk_ini of additional settings (exact keys not documented here; unknown).
cb may be null; if provided, must match on_mk_media_send_rtp_result signature.
user_data must remain valid until the operation completes or the callback is cleared.

functions.name: mk_media_start_send_rtp4
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_start_send_rtp4(mk_media ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, const char *ssrc, int con_type, mk_ini options, on_mk_media_send_rtp_result cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Start sending PS-over-RTP with mk_ini options and a user_data destructor. Thread-safe.
requirements: Same as mk_media_start_send_rtp3 for ctx, dst_url, dst_port, ssrc, con_type, options.
user_data may be null; if non-null, it must remain valid until user_data_free is called by the library.
user_data_free may be null; if provided, it must be safe to call exactly once by the library.

functions.name: mk_media_stop_send_rtp
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_media_stop_send_rtp(mk_media ctx, const char *ssrc);
functions.description: Stop sending one PS-over-RTP stream matching the given SSRC or stop all RTP outputs if ssrc is null or an empty string. Thread-safe.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
ssrc is a decimal string SSRC; if null or empty, all RTP sending for this media will be stopped.
This API is documented as thread-safe.

functions.name: mk_media_get_owner_thread
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_thread API_CALL mk_media_get_owner_thread(mk_media ctx);
functions.description: Return the thread object that owns this media source, for thread-affinity operations or posting tasks to the owner thread.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_media handle.
Returned mk_thread is an opaque handle; use mk_thread APIs for interaction (details not included here).

functions.name: mk_player_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_player API_CALL mk_player_create();
functions.description: Create a player instance supporting RTMP/RTMPS and RTSP/RTSPS playback. Returns an opaque mk_player handle to be used with other player APIs.
requirements: Must be called before any other mk_player_* function that requires a valid player handle.
The returned mk_player must later be released with mk_player_release to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: mk_player_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_release(mk_player ctx);
functions.description: Destroy and free a player instance previously created by mk_player_create. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player returned by mk_player_create.
After calling, ctx becomes invalid and must not be reused.
All associated callbacks will be considered unregistered after release.

functions.name: mk_player_set_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_set_option(mk_player ctx, const char *key, const char *val);
functions.description: Set a configuration option on the player. Supported keys include: net_adapter, rtp_type, rtsp_user, rtsp_pwd, protocol_timeout_ms, media_timeout_ms, beat_interval_ms, wait_track_ready. Values must be provided as strings (convert integers to string).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
key must name a supported option as documented (net_adapter/rtp_type/rtsp_user/rtsp_pwd/protocol_timeout_ms/media_timeout_ms/beat_interval_ms/wait_track_ready).
val must be a null-terminated string; if the underlying type is integer, it must be string-encoded.
Should be set before starting playback with mk_player_play for the options to take effect (not explicitly stated but typical).

functions.name: mk_player_play
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_play(mk_player ctx, const char *url);
functions.description: Start playback of the specified media URL over RTSP(S) or RTMP(S). Initiates connection and playback; result and interruption are delivered via the registered callbacks.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
url must be a null-terminated string using rtsp://, rtsps://, rtmp://, or rtmps:// scheme.

For result/shutdown notifications, register callbacks with mk_player_set_on_result(_2) and mk_player_set_on_shutdown(_2) before calling this function for them to capture initial events (recommended; not strictly enforced by signature).

functions.name: mk_player_pause
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_pause(mk_player ctx, int pause);
functions.description: Pause or resume playback. Only meaningful for on-demand (VOD) streams.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
pause must be 1 to pause or 0 to resume.
Has effect only for on-demand content; calling on live streams may have no effect.

functions.name: mk_player_speed
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_speed(mk_player ctx, float speed);
functions.description: Adjust playback speed for on-demand (VOD) streams. Typical values mentioned are 0.5, 1.0, 2.0.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
Effective only for on-demand content; may have no effect for live streams.
speed is a floating-point playback multiplier; specific allowed range beyond the examples is not specified.

functions.name: mk_player_seekto
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_seekto(mk_player ctx, float progress);
functions.description: Seek within on-demand content by normalized progress. The value range is 0.0 to 1.0, representing the relative position within the media.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
progress must be in the range [0.0, 1.0].
Applies to on-demand content; semantics for live streams are not defined.

functions.name: mk_player_seekto_pos
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_seekto_pos(mk_player ctx, int seek_pos);
functions.description: Seek within on-demand content to a position specified as an offset from the start time, in seconds.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
seek_pos is an integer offset in seconds relative to the start time; exact bounds are not specified in the header.
Applies to on-demand content; semantics for live streams are not defined.

functions.name: mk_player_set_on_result
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_set_on_result(mk_player ctx, on_mk_play_event cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register or clear the callback for playback result events (initial success or failure). Passing null as cb cancels the callback. The callback receives error code/message and track list on success.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
cb may be null to cancel the callback; otherwise must match on_mk_play_event signature.
user_data is passed back to cb as provided; the library does not free it in this variant.

functions.name: mk_player_set_on_result2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_set_on_result2(mk_player ctx, on_mk_play_event cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register or clear the playback result callback with a custom destructor for user_data. Passing null as cb cancels the callback. When the library discards the callback, it will invoke user_data_free on user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
cb may be null to cancel the callback; otherwise must match on_mk_play_event signature.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer compatible with freeing user_data; it may be called by the library to release user_data.

functions.name: mk_player_set_on_shutdown
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_set_on_shutdown(mk_player ctx, on_mk_play_event cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register or clear the callback invoked when playback is abnormally interrupted (shutdown). Passing null as cb cancels the callback. Only after playback success are media info interfaces valid.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
cb may be null to cancel the callback; otherwise must match on_mk_play_event signature.
user_data is passed back to cb as provided; the library does not free it in this variant.

functions.name: mk_player_set_on_shutdown2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_player_set_on_shutdown2(mk_player ctx, on_mk_play_event cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register or clear the shutdown (abnormal interruption) callback with a custom destructor for user_data. Passing null as cb cancels the callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
cb may be null to cancel the callback; otherwise must match on_mk_play_event signature.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer compatible with freeing user_data; it may be called by the library to release user_data.

functions.name: mk_player_duration
functions.signature: API_EXPORT float API_CALL mk_player_duration(mk_player ctx);
functions.description: Get the on-demand program duration in seconds. Returns 0 for live streams. Valid only after the playback success callback has been triggered.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
Only valid after a successful playback result event has occurred; before that, the value may be invalid/unspecified.
For live streams the function returns 0 by design.

functions.name: mk_player_progress
functions.signature: API_EXPORT float API_CALL mk_player_progress(mk_player ctx);
functions.description: Get normalized on-demand playback progress in the range 0.0 to 1.0. Valid only after the playback success callback has been triggered.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
Only valid after a successful playback result event has occurred.
Return value is defined for on-demand content; behavior for live streams is not specified.

functions.name: mk_player_progress_pos
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_player_progress_pos(mk_player ctx);
functions.description: Get on-demand playback position as an offset relative to the start time, in seconds. Valid only after the playback success callback has been triggered.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
Only valid after a successful playback result event has occurred.
Return value is an integer number of seconds relative to start; exact range is not specified.

functions.name: mk_player_loss_rate
functions.signature: API_EXPORT float API_CALL mk_player_loss_rate(mk_player ctx, int track_type);
functions.description: Get RTSP packet loss rate for a specific track. track_type 0 selects video, 1 selects audio. Only applicable/valid for RTSP playback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_player.
track_type must be 0 for video or 1 for audio.
Meaningful only for RTSP/RTSPS playback; behavior for RTMP is not defined.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_proxy_player API_CALL mk_proxy_player_create(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, int hls_enabled, int mp4_enabled);
functions.description: Create a proxy player instance bound to the specified vhost/app/stream and configure whether to generate HLS and/or MP4 outputs. Use the returned opaque handle with other mk_proxy_player_* APIs, then release it with mk_proxy_player_release. Note: Although older comments reference rtp_type, this function’s signature has no rtp_type parameter; RTP type can be adjusted later via mk_proxy_player_set_option using key "rtp_type".
requirements: vhost must be a valid, null-terminated C string (commonly "__defaultVhost__").
app must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
stream must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
hls_enabled is a flag (0 disables, non-zero enables) inferred from docs.
mp4_enabled is a flag (0 disables, non-zero enables) inferred from docs.
The returned mk_proxy_player handle must be released with mk_proxy_player_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_create2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_proxy_player API_CALL mk_proxy_player_create2(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, mk_ini option);
functions.description: Create a proxy player instance using a ProtocolOption configuration (mk_ini) instead of discrete flags. Use this when you need finer protocol-related control. The returned handle is used with other APIs and must be released with mk_proxy_player_release.
requirements: vhost must be a valid, null-terminated C string (commonly "__defaultVhost__").
app must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
stream must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
option must be a valid/initialized mk_ini carrying ProtocolOption-related configuration (exact keys not defined here).
The returned mk_proxy_player handle must be released with mk_proxy_player_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_create3
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_proxy_player API_CALL mk_proxy_player_create3(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, int hls_enabled, int mp4_enabled, int retry_count);
functions.description: Create a proxy player instance like mk_proxy_player_create while also specifying an automatic reconnect retry count. A negative retry_count causes infinite retries. Use the handle with other mk_proxy_player_* APIs; release with mk_proxy_player_release.
requirements: vhost must be a valid, null-terminated C string (commonly "__defaultVhost__").
app must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
stream must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
hls_enabled is a flag (0 disables, non-zero enables) inferred from docs.
mp4_enabled is a flag (0 disables, non-zero enables) inferred from docs.
retry_count < 0 means retry infinitely; otherwise, the number of retries attempted is retry_count.
The returned mk_proxy_player handle must be released with mk_proxy_player_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_create4
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_proxy_player API_CALL mk_proxy_player_create4(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, mk_ini option, int retry_count);
functions.description: Create a proxy player instance using ProtocolOption (mk_ini) plus a reconnect retry policy. A negative retry_count causes infinite retries. Use the handle with other APIs and release it with mk_proxy_player_release.
requirements: vhost must be a valid, null-terminated C string (commonly "__defaultVhost__").
app must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
stream must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
option must be a valid/initialized mk_ini containing ProtocolOption configuration.
retry_count < 0 means retry infinitely; otherwise, the number of retries attempted is retry_count.
The returned mk_proxy_player handle must be released with mk_proxy_player_release when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_release(mk_proxy_player ctx);
functions.description: Destroy and free a proxy player created by one of the mk_proxy_player_create* functions. After calling this, the handle and any associated resources must not be used. Typically invoked when handling MediaSource.close() or when the player is no longer needed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle obtained from mk_proxy_player_create* and not already released.
After return, the caller must not use ctx again (dangling handle).
If set_on_close was registered to handle MediaSource.close(), callers should invoke this within that callback as instructed by the header comments.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_set_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_set_option(mk_proxy_player ctx, const char *key, const char *val);
functions.description: Set a string-based configuration option on the proxy player. Supported keys include: net_adapter, rtp_type, rtsp_user, rtsp_pwd, protocol_timeout_ms, media_timeout_ms, beat_interval_ms, rtsp_speed. Integer values must be provided as strings.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.
key must be a valid, null-terminated C string and one of the supported keys listed in the header.
val must be a valid, null-terminated C string; if representing an integer, convert it to a string before passing.
Behavior for unsupported keys is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_play
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_play(mk_proxy_player ctx, const char *url);
functions.description: Start playback for the proxy player from the specified URL. The URL scheme is documented to support rtsp/rtmp. Use callbacks (e.g., on_play_result) to observe initial play success/failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.
url must be a valid, null-terminated C string; documented to support rtsp and rtmp schemes.
If the application needs to respond to first-play success/failure, register mk_proxy_player_set_on_play_result before initiating playback (recommended usage inferred from docs).

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_set_on_close
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_set_on_close(mk_proxy_player ctx, on_mk_proxy_player_cb cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback to listen for MediaSource.close() events associated with this proxy player. When triggered, you should release the proxy player (mk_proxy_player_release) and free related resources. The user_data is passed back when the callback is invoked.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.
cb must be a function pointer of type on_mk_proxy_player_cb; it will be invoked with (user_data, err, what, sys_err) when MediaSource.close() occurs.
user_data can be any pointer supplied by the caller; it will be passed through to the callback. Memory management of user_data is the caller’s responsibility (no automatic free in this variant).

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_set_on_close2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_set_on_close2(mk_proxy_player ctx, on_mk_proxy_player_cb cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a MediaSource.close() callback with an accompanying user-data free callback. The user_data pointer is returned to the cb when invoked, and user_data_free is used by the library to release user_data at the appropriate time.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.
cb must be a function pointer of type on_mk_proxy_player_cb; it will be invoked with (user_data, err, what, sys_err) when MediaSource.close() occurs.
user_data can be any pointer supplied by the caller; it will be passed to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer of type on_user_data_free that can safely dispose the provided user_data when the library decides to free it (exact timing unspecified in this header).

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_set_on_play_result
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_proxy_player_set_on_play_result(mk_proxy_player ctx, on_mk_proxy_player_cb cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a callback to receive the result of the first playback attempt. If the first play fails, it is considered a startup failure. The callback receives user_data and error information; user_data_free is used by the library to release user_data when appropriate.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.
cb must be a function pointer of type on_mk_proxy_player_cb; it will be invoked with (user_data, err, what, sys_err) to report the first play result.
user_data can be any pointer supplied by the caller; it will be passed to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer of type on_user_data_free to dispose of user_data when the library frees it (exact timing unspecified in this header).
For observing first-play success/failure, register this callback before calling mk_proxy_player_play (recommended usage inferred from docs).

functions.name: mk_proxy_player_total_reader_count
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_proxy_player_total_reader_count(mk_proxy_player ctx);
functions.description: Return the total number of viewers currently consuming the proxied media associated with this player.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_proxy_player handle.

functions.name: mk_pusher_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_pusher API_CALL mk_pusher_create(const char *schema, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream);
functions.description: Create an RTMP(S)/RTSP(S) pusher bound to an existing, registered MediaSource identified by schema/vhost/app/stream. Use this when you know the MediaSource’s identifiers and need a pusher handle to publish it to a remote URL.
requirements: schema must be either "rtsp" or "rtmp" (per documented support).
The referenced MediaSource (vhost/app/stream) must already exist and be registered before this call.
vhost, app, and stream must point to null-terminated strings.
Returns a non-null mk_pusher on success; caller must release it with mk_pusher_release when done.
Do not use the returned mk_pusher after it has been released.

functions.name: mk_pusher_create_src
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_pusher API_CALL mk_pusher_create_src(mk_media_source src);
functions.description: Create an RTMP(S)/RTSP(S) pusher bound directly to a given MediaSource handle. Use when you already have an mk_media_source and want to push it.
requirements: src must be a valid mk_media_source referring to a MediaSource that is already registered.
Returns a non-null mk_pusher on success; caller must release it with mk_pusher_release when done.
Do not use the returned mk_pusher after it has been released.

functions.name: mk_pusher_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_release(mk_pusher ctx);
functions.description: Release and destroy a pusher created by mk_pusher_create or mk_pusher_create_src. After releasing, the handle becomes invalid.
requirements: ctx must be a pusher previously obtained from mk_pusher_create or mk_pusher_create_src.
Each mk_pusher must be released exactly once to avoid leaks or double-free.
Do not use ctx after this call returns.

functions.name: mk_pusher_set_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_set_option(mk_pusher ctx, const char *key, const char *val);
functions.description: Set a configuration option on the pusher. Supported keys include: net_adapter, rtp_type, rtsp_user, rtsp_pwd, protocol_timeout_ms, media_timeout_ms, beat_interval_ms. Values are passed as strings.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher.
key must be one of the supported option names documented in the header.
val must be a null-terminated string; if the logical value is an integer, it must be provided as a string.
Options should be set before starting publish with mk_pusher_publish for them to take effect (implied by typical configuration flow).

functions.name: mk_pusher_publish
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_publish(mk_pusher ctx, const char *url);
functions.description: Start pushing the bound MediaSource to the specified URL. Supported schemes are rtsp, rtsps, rtmp, rtmps.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher created and not yet released.
url must be a valid null-terminated URL string with scheme rtsp[s] or rtmp[s].
The associated MediaSource must remain valid/registered for the duration of the push.
If result/shutdown callbacks are desired, set them before initiating publish.

functions.name: mk_pusher_set_on_result
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_set_on_result(mk_pusher ctx, on_mk_push_event cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback to receive the streaming result event. The callback is invoked with err_code (0 indicates success) and an error message. Suitable for receiving the outcome of mk_pusher_publish.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher.
cb must not be NULL.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; the caller retains ownership and must manage its lifetime.

functions.name: mk_pusher_set_on_result2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_set_on_result2(mk_pusher ctx, on_mk_push_event cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a streaming result callback with an additional destructor for user_data. The callback reports publish result (err_code 0 on success) or errors; user_data_free will be called by the library to release user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher.
cb must not be NULL.
user_data may be NULL or any pointer; it will be passed to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer if provided; it will be invoked by the library to free user_data (caller must ensure it is safe to call exactly as the library expects).

functions.name: mk_pusher_set_on_shutdown
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_set_on_shutdown(mk_pusher ctx, on_mk_push_event cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback for abnormal streaming interruption (shutdown). The callback receives an error code and message describing why the push stopped unexpectedly.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher.
cb must not be NULL.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; the caller retains ownership and must manage its lifetime.

functions.name: mk_pusher_set_on_shutdown2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_pusher_set_on_shutdown2(mk_pusher ctx, on_mk_push_event cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a shutdown (abnormal interruption) callback with an additional destructor for user_data. When the push is interrupted, cb is invoked; the library will later call user_data_free to release user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_pusher.
cb must not be NULL.
user_data may be NULL or any pointer; it will be passed to cb.
user_data_free must be a valid function pointer if provided; it will be invoked by the library to free user_data (caller must ensure it matches the allocation of user_data).

functions.name: mk_flv_recorder_create
functions.signature: mk_flv_recorder API_CALL mk_flv_recorder_create(void);
functions.description: Create an FLV recorder instance and return an opaque handle for subsequent FLV recording operations. Use together with mk_flv_recorder_start and release with mk_flv_recorder_release when finished.
requirements: Must be released with mk_flv_recorder_release to avoid resource leaks.
Returned handle must be checked for NULL before use; behavior on allocation failure is unknown (not documented).

functions.name: mk_flv_recorder_release
functions.signature: void API_CALL mk_flv_recorder_release(mk_flv_recorder ctx);
functions.description: Release and destroy a previously created FLV recorder handle created by mk_flv_recorder_create. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_flv_recorder returned by mk_flv_recorder_create.
Do not use ctx after release (dangling handle).
Calling release exactly once per created recorder is required; double-free is invalid (not documented but implied).

functions.name: mk_flv_recorder_start
functions.signature: int API_CALL mk_flv_recorder_start(mk_flv_recorder ctx, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, const char *file_path);
functions.description: Start recording an existing RtmpMediaSource stream to an FLV file. Identifies the source by vhost/app/stream and writes to file_path.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_flv_recorder created by mk_flv_recorder_create and not yet released.
vhost, app, stream, and file_path must be valid, null-terminated strings.
The identified RtmpMediaSource must exist; otherwise the function fails and returns -1 (per comment).
Target file_path must be creatable/writable; file open failure causes return -1.
Return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure (file open failure or source does not exist).

functions.name: mk_recorder_is_recording
functions.signature: int API_CALL mk_recorder_is_recording(int type, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream);
functions.description: Query whether recording is active for a given stream and recording type.
requirements: type must be 0 (HLS) or 1 (MP4).
vhost, app, and stream must be valid, null-terminated strings that identify the stream.
Return value: 0 means not recording; 1 means recording.

functions.name: mk_recorder_start
functions.signature: int API_CALL mk_recorder_start(int type, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, const char *customized_path, size_t max_second);
functions.description: Start recording for the specified stream and format. Supports HLS-TS, MP4, HLS-FMP4, HTTP-FMP4, and HTTP-TS. Optionally provide a custom save directory and the maximum MP4 segment duration.
requirements: type must be one of: 0 (hls-ts), 1 (MP4), 2 (hls-fmp4), 3 (http-fmp4), 4 (http-ts).
vhost, app, and stream must be valid, null-terminated strings that identify the stream.
customized_path may be NULL or empty to auto-generate the save directory; otherwise it must be a valid path string.
max_second is in seconds; set to 0 to use configuration defaults; otherwise must be a non-negative size (size_t).
Return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: mk_recorder_stop
functions.signature: int API_CALL mk_recorder_stop(int type, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream);
functions.description: Stop an ongoing recording for the specified stream and recording type.
requirements: type must be one of: 0 (hls-ts), 1 (MP4), 2 (hls-fmp4), 3 (http-fmp4), 4 (http-ts).
vhost, app, and stream must be valid, null-terminated strings that identify the stream being recorded.
Return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: mk_recorder_start_task
functions.signature: int API_CALL mk_recorder_start_task(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, const char *path, uint32_t back_ms, uint32_t forward_ms);
functions.description: Start an event-based video recording task that captures data from back_ms milliseconds before the request and continues for forward_ms milliseconds after. Saves to the provided relative path including filename.
requirements: vhost, app, stream, and path must be valid, null-terminated strings.
path is a relative save path including the file name (per comment).
back_ms and forward_ms are durations in milliseconds and must fit in 32-bit unsigned integers; negative values are invalid.
Return value: 1 indicates success; 0 indicates failure.

functions.name: mk_load_mp4_file
functions.signature: void API_CALL mk_load_mp4_file(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, const char *file_path, int file_repeat);
functions.description: Load or inject an MP4 file (or list) into a stream context for processing/demuxing. file_repeat controls looping demux.
requirements: vhost, app, stream, and file_path must be valid, null-terminated strings.
file_path must refer to an accessible MP4 file (or list) path.
file_repeat controls loop demux; treat 0 as no loop and non-zero as loop (per comment implication).
No return value; callers cannot directly detect failure from this API.

functions.name: mk_load_mp4_file2
functions.signature: void API_CALL mk_load_mp4_file2(const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream, const char *file_path, int file_repeat, mk_ini ini);
functions.description: Load or inject an MP4 file (or list) into a stream context for processing/demuxing with additional configuration provided via ini.
requirements: vhost, app, stream, and file_path must be valid, null-terminated strings.
file_path must refer to an accessible MP4 file (or list) path.
file_repeat controls loop demux; treat 0 as no loop and non-zero as loop (per comment implication).
ini must be a valid mk_ini configuration object from mk_util.h; exact required keys are not documented.
No return value; callers cannot directly detect failure from this API.

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_create
functions.signature: mk_rtp_server mk_rtp_server_create(uint16_t port, int tcp_mode, const char *stream_id);
functions.description: Create a GB28181 RTP server bound to a specific stream ID. Use tcp_mode to choose behavior: 0 = do not listen, 1 = listen on the given port, 2 = TCP active (client) mode. Port 0 requests a random available port. Intended for setting up an RTP receiver endpoint for a single stream.
requirements: port must be in uint16_t range; a value of 0 requests a random port
tcp_mode must be one of: 0 (no listening), 1 (listen), 2 (active connect mode)
stream_id must be a valid null-terminated C string
The returned mk_rtp_server must be released with mk_rtp_server_release when no longer needed

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_create2
functions.signature: mk_rtp_server mk_rtp_server_create2(uint16_t port, int tcp_mode, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream_id);
functions.description: Create a GB28181 RTP server with explicit vhost/app/stream identifiers. tcp_mode: 0 = do not listen, 1 = listen, 2 = TCP active (client) mode. Port 0 requests a random available port.
requirements: port must be in uint16_t range; a value of 0 requests a random port
tcp_mode must be one of: 0 (no listening), 1 (listen), 2 (active connect mode)
vhost, app, and stream_id must be valid null-terminated C strings
The returned mk_rtp_server must be released with mk_rtp_server_release when no longer needed

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_create3
functions.signature: mk_rtp_server mk_rtp_server_create3(uint16_t port, int tcp_mode, const char *vhost, const char *app, const char *stream_id, int multiplex);
functions.description: Create a GB28181 RTP server with vhost/app/stream and a multiplex switch. tcp_mode: 0 = do not listen, 1 = listen, 2 = TCP active (client) mode. Port 0 requests a random available port. multiplex controls multi-session RTP on the same server: 1 = enabled, 0 = disabled.
requirements: port must be in uint16_t range; a value of 0 requests a random port
tcp_mode must be one of: 0 (no listening), 1 (listen), 2 (active connect mode)
vhost, app, and stream_id must be valid null-terminated C strings
multiplex must be 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled)
The returned mk_rtp_server must be released with mk_rtp_server_release when no longer needed

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_connect
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_connect(mk_rtp_server ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, on_mk_rtp_server_connected cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: In TCP active mode, initiate a connection from the RTP server to a remote server. Invokes the provided callback to report success or failure, passing back user_data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server previously created (typically with tcp_mode = 2 for active mode)
dst_url must be a valid null-terminated server address string
dst_port must be in uint16_t range
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked to report connection result
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to cb; caller must keep it valid until the callback is invoked or the operation is canceled/released

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_connect2
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_connect2(mk_rtp_server ctx, const char *dst_url, uint16_t dst_port, on_mk_rtp_server_connected cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Like mk_rtp_server_connect but also accepts a user_data_free callback for releasing user_data when the library is done with it.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server previously created (typically with tcp_mode = 2 for active mode)
dst_url must be a valid null-terminated server address string
dst_port must be in uint16_t range
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked to report connection result
user_data is an opaque pointer passed back to cb
user_data_free, if provided, must be callable to free user_data; it may be called by the library to release user_data

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_release
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_release(mk_rtp_server ctx);
functions.description: Destroy and free a GB28181 RTP server created by mk_rtp_server_create/2/3.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server obtained from a create function
After calling, ctx must not be used again

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_port
functions.signature: uint16_t mk_rtp_server_port(mk_rtp_server ctx);
functions.description: Return the local listening port number of the RTP server.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_set_on_detach
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_set_on_detach(mk_rtp_server ctx, on_mk_rtp_server_detach cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a callback to be notified when the GB28181 RTP server times out waiting for incoming RTP (receive-stream timeout). user_data is passed back to the callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server
cb must be a valid function pointer
user_data is an opaque pointer that must remain valid for the lifetime of the registration or until replaced

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_set_on_detach2
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_set_on_detach2(mk_rtp_server ctx, on_mk_rtp_server_detach cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a receive-stream timeout callback with an additional user_data_free function to release user_data when no longer needed.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server
cb must be a valid function pointer
user_data is an opaque pointer passed to the callback
user_data_free, if provided, must be callable to free user_data; it may be invoked by the library

functions.name: mk_rtp_server_update_ssrc
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_server_update_ssrc(mk_rtp_server ctx, uint32_t ssrc);
functions.description: Update the RTP server’s SSRC filter to the specified SSRC value (comment notes the value as decimal).
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_rtp_server
ssrc is the desired SSRC value as a uint32_t

functions.name: mk_rtp_get_info
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_get_info(const char *app, const char *stream, on_mk_rtp_get_info cb);
functions.description: Query RTP push-stream information for the given app and stream. The callback receives whether info exists (exist: 0/1), peer/local IP and port, and an identifier string.
requirements: app and stream must be valid null-terminated C strings
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with the query result

functions.name: mk_rtp_pause_check
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_pause_check(const char *app, const char *stream);
functions.description: Pause RTP timeout checking for the specified app and stream.
requirements: app and stream must be valid null-terminated C strings

functions.name: mk_rtp_resume_check
functions.signature: void mk_rtp_resume_check(const char *app, const char *stream);
functions.description: Resume RTP timeout checking for the specified app and stream.
requirements: app and stream must be valid null-terminated C strings

functions.name: mk_buffer_from_char
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_buffer API_CALL mk_buffer_from_char(const char *data, size_t len, on_mk_buffer_free cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Create an mk_buffer from a raw memory region. If cb is null, the implementation will copy the provided data internally; otherwise, the buffer will reference the provided data and invoke cb(user_data, data) upon buffer release.
requirements: data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory.
If cb is null, len defines the number of bytes to copy.
If cb is non-null, the caller must ensure data remains valid until the buffer is released (the buffer will not copy the data) and be prepared for cb to be invoked to free or finalize the data.
user_data is passed as-is to the on_mk_buffer_free callback; its lifetime management is up to the caller unless a different API takes ownership.
Returned mk_buffer is an opaque handle that should be released with mk_buffer_unref when no longer needed.

functions.name: mk_buffer_from_char2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_buffer API_CALL mk_buffer_from_char2(const char *data, size_t len, on_mk_buffer_free cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Create an mk_buffer from a raw memory region with an additional destructor for user_data.
