requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Ownership of the returned string and its lifetime are unknown; treat as read-only and do not free.

functions.name: mk_track_bit_rate
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_bit_rate(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the track's bitrate information. Units and whether this is instantaneous or average are not specified.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Units (bps, kbps) and value semantics are unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_ready
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_ready(mk_track track);
functions.description: Return whether the track is ready: 1 for ready, 0 for not ready.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Only boolean-like values 0 or 1 are documented.

functions.name: mk_track_frames
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_track_frames(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the cumulative number of frames processed by the track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Exact counting semantics (decoded, encoded, keyframes-only) are not specified; inferred as total frames.

functions.name: mk_track_duration
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_track_duration(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the elapsed duration for the track in milliseconds.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Whether this is wall-clock or media-time and the start reference are unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_add_delegate
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void *API_CALL mk_track_add_delegate(mk_track track, on_mk_frame_out cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a frame output callback for the track. The callback is invoked when frames are output. Returns an opaque tag pointer to manage this registration (e.g., for later removal).
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
cb is a function pointer of type on_mk_frame_out that will be called with user_data and a mk_frame; whether cb may be NULL is unknown.
user_data is passed back to the callback; its lifetime management is the caller's responsibility.
Store the returned tag to later remove the delegate with mk_track_del_delegate.
Threading and callback invocation context are unknown; callbacks should be reentrant-safe.

functions.name: mk_track_add_delegate2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void *API_CALL mk_track_add_delegate2(mk_track track, on_mk_frame_out cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a frame output callback with an optional user-data finalizer. Returns an opaque tag pointer for managing the registration. When the delegate is removed or the track is destroyed, user_data_free may be invoked to release user_data.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
cb is a function pointer of type on_mk_frame_out; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
user_data is an opaque pointer passed to cb.
user_data_free is a function pointer of type on_user_data_free used to clean up user_data; exact invocation time and threading are unknown.
Store the returned tag to later remove the delegate with mk_track_del_delegate.

functions.name: mk_track_del_delegate
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_track_del_delegate(mk_track track, void *tag);
functions.description: Unregister a previously added frame output callback using the tag returned by mk_track_add_delegate or mk_track_add_delegate2.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
tag must be the exact opaque pointer returned by mk_track_add_delegate(2).
Behavior when tag is invalid or already removed is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_input_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_track_input_frame(mk_track track, mk_frame frame);
functions.description: Input a frame into the track. Typically not needed by most users; intended for low-level or custom feeding of frames.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
frame must be a valid mk_frame, presumably compatible with the track's codec; exact compatibility requirements are unknown.
Ownership and lifetime of frame during and after the call are unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_is_video
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_is_video(mk_track track);
functions.description: Return whether the track is a video track (nonzero) or not (zero).
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
Return value is treated as boolean (0/1), but any nonzero may indicate true; only 0/1 is documented elsewhere.

functions.name: mk_track_video_width
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_video_width(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the video width for a video track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_video_height
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_video_height(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the video height for a video track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_video_fps
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_video_fps(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the video frame rate (frames per second) for a video track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.
Units are frames per second; whether fractional fps is supported is unknown (integer return).

functions.name: mk_track_video_key_frames
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_track_video_key_frames(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the cumulative number of video keyframes observed for the track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_video_gop_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_video_gop_size(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the video GOP (keyframe interval) size in frames.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.
Exact definition (average vs. current GOP) is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_video_gop_interval_ms
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_video_gop_interval_ms(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the video keyframe interval in milliseconds (cumulative measure).
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-video track, behavior is unknown.
Whether this is an average, last, or configured interval is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_audio_sample_rate
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_audio_sample_rate(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the audio sample rate for an audio track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-audio track, behavior is unknown.
Units are samples per second.

functions.name: mk_track_audio_channel
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_audio_channel(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the number of audio channels for an audio track.
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-audio track, behavior is unknown.

functions.name: mk_track_audio_sample_bit
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_track_audio_sample_bit(mk_track track);
functions.description: Get the audio bit depth (typically 16 bits).
requirements: track must be a valid mk_track.
If called on a non-audio track, behavior is unknown.
Returned bit depth is implementation-defined; commonly 16.

functions.name: mk_decoder_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_decoder API_CALL mk_decoder_create(mk_track track, int thread_num);
functions.description: Create a decoder bound to the specified media track. Use when you need to decode compressed frames from a mk_track. thread_num controls decoder thread count; 0 selects an automatic/default value. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: track must reference a valid mk_track describing the encoded stream to be decoded.
thread_num == 0 enables automatic thread selection; behavior for other values is implementation-defined.
Callers must check the return for NULL before use.
The returned mk_decoder must be released with mk_decoder_release.

functions.name: mk_decoder_create2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_decoder API_CALL mk_decoder_create2(mk_track track, int thread_num, const char *codec_name_list[]);
functions.description: Create a decoder with an optional preferred FFmpeg codec list. Use to influence decoder selection (e.g., hardware decoders). The codec list must be NULL-terminated; if unavailable or incompatible with the track codec id, an internal default list is used. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: track must reference a valid mk_track for the encoded stream.
thread_num == 0 enables automatic thread selection; behavior for other values is implementation-defined.
codec_name_list, if provided, must be a NULL-terminated array of C strings (e.g., {"libopenh264", "h264_nvdec", NULL}).
If specified codec(s) do not exist or do not match mk_track's codec id, the internal default codec selection is used.
Callers must check the return for NULL before use.
The returned mk_decoder must be released with mk_decoder_release.

functions.name: mk_decoder_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_decoder_release(mk_decoder ctx,  int flush_frame);
functions.description: Destroy a decoder and release its resources. Optionally wait for all queued frames to finish decoding before destruction.
requirements: ctx must be a decoder created by mk_decoder_create or mk_decoder_create2, and not previously released.
flush_frame controls whether to wait for all frames to be decoded (non-zero to wait).
Do not use ctx after this call.

functions.name: mk_decoder_decode
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_decoder_decode(mk_decoder ctx, mk_frame frame, int async, int enable_merge);
functions.description: Submit an encoded audio/video frame to the decoder. Can operate asynchronously and optionally merge slices with identical timestamps before decoding when required by some bitstreams.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_decoder.
frame must be a valid mk_frame containing encoded data compatible with ctx.
async indicates asynchronous decoding when non-zero; synchronous when zero.
enable_merge enables slice merging when non-zero for streams that require it.
If asynchronous, application should be prepared to receive decoded output via the registered callback.

functions.name: mk_decoder_set_max_async_frame_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_decoder_set_max_async_frame_size(mk_decoder ctx, size_t size);
functions.description: Set the maximum backlog (count) of frames cached for asynchronous decoding to limit buffering.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_decoder.
size specifies the maximum number of frames to buffer asynchronously; larger values increase memory usage.
Only affects asynchronous decoding behavior.

functions.name: mk_decoder_set_cb
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_decoder_set_cb(mk_decoder ctx, on_mk_decode cb, void *user_data);
functions.description: Register a decode output callback invoked with each decoded mk_frame_pix. user_data is passed back unmodified to the callback.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_decoder.
cb may be NULL to clear the callback; if non-NULL it must conform to on_mk_decode(void *user_data, mk_frame_pix frame).
user_data is an opaque pointer provided by the caller; its lifetime must outlive the period during which callbacks may occur.
Callbacks may be invoked from internal decoding threads if async decoding is enabled; user code must be thread-safe.

functions.name: mk_decoder_set_cb2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_decoder_set_cb2(mk_decoder ctx, on_mk_decode cb, void *user_data, on_user_data_free user_data_free);
functions.description: Register a decode output callback with an optional user_data destructor. When the decoder no longer needs user_data, user_data_free will be called to release it.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_decoder.
cb may be NULL to clear the callback.
user_data is an opaque pointer; ensure it remains valid until user_data_free is invoked.
user_data_free, if non-NULL, must be a valid function matching on_user_data_free to properly release user_data.
Callbacks may occur on internal threads; user code and user_data_free must be thread-safe.

functions.name: mk_decoder_get_context
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const AVCodecContext* API_CALL mk_decoder_get_context(mk_decoder ctx);
functions.description: Retrieve the underlying FFmpeg AVCodecContext associated with the decoder for advanced configuration/introspection. Returned pointer is const and owned by the decoder.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_decoder.
The returned AVCodecContext pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller.
The pointer becomes invalid once the decoder is released.

functions.name: mk_frame_pix_ref
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame_pix API_CALL mk_frame_pix_ref(mk_frame_pix frame);
functions.description: Create a new reference to a decoded pixel frame object (mk_frame_pix). Increments internal reference so multiple holders can share the frame.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame_pix.
The returned reference must be released with mk_frame_pix_unref when no longer needed.
Reference counts must be balanced to avoid leaks.

functions.name: mk_frame_pix_unref
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_frame_pix_unref(mk_frame_pix frame);
functions.description: Release a reference to a mk_frame_pix. When the last reference is released, the underlying resources are freed.
requirements: frame must be a mk_frame_pix previously acquired (e.g., from a decode callback, mk_frame_pix_ref, mk_frame_pix_from_av_frame, or mk_swscale_input_frame2).
Do not use frame after unref.

functions.name: mk_frame_pix_from_av_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame_pix API_CALL mk_frame_pix_from_av_frame(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Wrap or convert an FFmpeg AVFrame into a mk_frame_pix object. Useful to interoperate with external FFmpeg code. Returns a new mk_frame_pix handle.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame pointer.
The returned mk_frame_pix must be released with mk_frame_pix_unref.
Ownership/aliasing of the AVFrame memory is implementation-defined; ensure the AVFrame remains valid if the wrapper references it without copying.

functions.name: mk_frame_pix_from_buffer
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame_pix API_CALL mk_frame_pix_from_buffer(mk_buffer plane_data[], int line_size[], int plane);
functions.description: Create a mk_frame_pix from external plane buffers without copying memory. Suitable for planar pixel formats where caller supplies per-plane data and line sizes.
requirements: plane_data must be an array of mk_buffer, one per plane; obtain raw pointers via mk_buffer_get_data when populating buffers.
line_size must be an array providing the stride for each plane.
plane specifies the number of data planes and must match the number of valid entries in plane_data and line_size.
Because no memory copy occurs, the underlying plane_data buffers must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the created mk_frame_pix.
The returned mk_frame_pix must be released with mk_frame_pix_unref.

functions.name: mk_frame_pix_get_av_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT AVFrame* API_CALL mk_frame_pix_get_av_frame(mk_frame_pix frame);
functions.description: Access the underlying FFmpeg AVFrame of a mk_frame_pix for direct FFmpeg operations.
requirements: frame must be a valid mk_frame_pix.
The returned AVFrame pointer is owned by the mk_frame_pix and must not be freed by the caller.
Pointer validity is tied to the lifetime of frame; do not use it after mk_frame_pix_unref.

functions.name: mk_swscale_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_swscale mk_swscale_create(int output, int width, int height);
functions.description: Create a wrapper around FFmpeg SwsContext to convert frames to a specified pixel format and optional target size. output is an AVPixelFormat value (e.g., AV_PIX_FMT_BGR24 == 3). width/height of 0 keep the input size.
requirements: output must be a valid AVPixelFormat integer value.
width and height may be 0 to inherit the input dimensions; positive values request scaling to that size.
The returned mk_swscale must be released with mk_swscale_release.

functions.name: mk_swscale_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void mk_swscale_release(mk_swscale ctx);
functions.description: Destroy a SwsContext wrapper and free associated resources.
requirements: ctx must be a mk_swscale created by mk_swscale_create and not previously released.
Do not use ctx after this call.

functions.name: mk_swscale_input_frame
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int mk_swscale_input_frame(mk_swscale ctx, mk_frame_pix frame, uint8_t *out);
functions.description: Convert a mk_frame_pix to the configured output pixel format (and size) using the swscale context, writing into a caller-provided buffer. Returns sws_scale() result: the height of the output slice.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_swscale created by mk_swscale_create.
frame must be a valid mk_frame_pix compatible with the scaler input.
out must point to a pre-allocated buffer large enough to hold the converted image; the caller must ensure size sufficiency.
Return value is the height of the output slice as per sws_scale().

functions.name: mk_swscale_input_frame2
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_frame_pix mk_swscale_input_frame2(mk_swscale ctx, mk_frame_pix frame);
functions.description: Convert a mk_frame_pix to the configured output pixel format (and size) and return a new mk_frame_pix containing the result. The caller must unref the returned frame.
requirements: ctx must be a valid mk_swscale created by mk_swscale_create.
frame must be a valid mk_frame_pix compatible with the scaler input.
The returned mk_frame_pix must be released with mk_frame_pix_unref.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_data
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint8_t **API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_data(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the AVFrame->data array pointer (per-plane data pointers).
requirements: frame must be a valid, initialized AVFrame.
The returned pointer refers to memory owned by the AVFrame; do not free it.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_data
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_data(AVFrame *frame, uint8_t *data, int plane);
functions.description: Set AVFrame->data[plane] to the provided data pointer.
requirements: frame must be a valid, initialized AVFrame.
plane is the plane index to set; it must denote a valid plane for the frame's format.
data must point to a buffer whose lifetime and layout matches the frame's format and dimensions.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_line_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int *API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_line_size(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get a pointer to AVFrame->linesize array (per-plane line sizes/strides).
requirements: frame must be a valid, initialized AVFrame.
The returned pointer refers to memory owned by the AVFrame; do not free it.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_line_size
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_line_size(AVFrame *frame, int line_size, int plane);
functions.description: Set AVFrame->linesize[plane] to line_size (stride in bytes).
requirements: frame must be a valid, initialized AVFrame.
plane is the plane index to set; it must denote a valid plane for the frame's format.
line_size must correspond to the buffer layout for the given plane.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_dts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int64_t API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_dts(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the decoding timestamp (DTS) from the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_dts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_dts(AVFrame *frame, int64_t dts);
functions.description: Set the decoding timestamp (DTS) on the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_pts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int64_t API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_pts(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the presentation timestamp (PTS) from the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_pts
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_pts(AVFrame *frame, int64_t pts);
functions.description: Set the presentation timestamp (PTS) on the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_width
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_width(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the frame width from the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_width
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_width(AVFrame *frame, int width);
functions.description: Set the frame width on the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.
width should match the actual buffer dimensions for consistency.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_height
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_height(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the frame height from the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_height
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_height(AVFrame *frame, int height);
functions.description: Set the frame height on the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.
height should match the actual buffer dimensions for consistency.

functions.name: mk_get_av_frame_format
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_get_av_frame_format(AVFrame *frame);
functions.description: Get the pixel/sample format (AVPixelFormat or AVSampleFormat as stored) from the AVFrame.
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.

functions.name: mk_set_av_frame_format
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_set_av_frame_format(AVFrame *frame, int format);
functions.description: Set the pixel/sample format on the AVFrame (expects the appropriate FFmpeg enum value).
requirements: frame must be a valid AVFrame.
format must be a valid FFmpeg format enum appropriate to the AVFrame type (e.g., AVPixelFormat for video).

functions.name: mk_free
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_free(void *ptr);
functions.description: Frees memory allocated internally by the mk API. Use this to release buffers returned by mk_* functions that document mk_free is required after use.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by an mk API function that documents mk_free should be used to free it.
Do not pass pointers you did not obtain from the mk API.
Callers should not use ptr after it has been freed.

functions.name: mk_util_get_exe_path
functions.signature: API_EXPORT char* API_CALL mk_util_get_exe_path();
functions.description: Returns the absolute path to the current process's executable. The returned buffer is heap-allocated by the mk API and must be freed by the caller using mk_free.
requirements: The returned pointer must be freed with mk_free when no longer needed.
Do not free the returned pointer with free or delete.

functions.name: mk_util_get_exe_dir
functions.signature: API_EXPORT char* API_CALL mk_util_get_exe_dir(const char *relative_path);
functions.description: Returns an absolute path derived from the directory containing the current executable. If relative_path is non-null, it is resolved relative to the executable's directory; if null, the path to the executable's directory is returned. The returned buffer is allocated by the mk API and must be freed with mk_free.
requirements: relative_path may be NULL.
The returned pointer must be freed with mk_free when no longer needed.
Do not free the returned pointer with free or delete.

functions.name: mk_util_get_current_millisecond
functions.signature: API_EXPORT uint64_t API_CALL mk_util_get_current_millisecond();
functions.description: Returns the current Unix timestamp in milliseconds according to the system clock. Useful for timing, logging, and generating time-based values.

functions.name: mk_util_get_current_time_string
functions.signature: API_EXPORT char* API_CALL mk_util_get_current_time_string(const char *fmt);
functions.description: Formats the current time according to the provided strftime-like format string (e.g., "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") and returns it as a newly allocated string. Caller must free the returned string with mk_free.
requirements: fmt should be a valid time format string compatible with strftime semantics.
The returned pointer must be freed with mk_free when no longer needed.
Do not free the returned pointer with free or delete.

functions.name: mk_util_hex_dump
functions.signature: API_EXPORT char* API_CALL mk_util_hex_dump(const void *buf, int len);
functions.description: Converts binary data into a printable debug string (hex dump). Returns a newly allocated string that must be freed with mk_free.
requirements: buf should point to a readable memory buffer of at least len bytes when len > 0.
len should be >= 0.
The returned pointer must be freed with mk_free when no longer needed.
Do not free the returned pointer with free or delete.

functions.name: mk_ini_create
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_ini API_CALL mk_ini_create();
functions.description: Creates a new, mutable INI configuration object. Use with other mk_ini_* functions to load, modify, and export configuration data. Release with mk_ini_release when done.
requirements: The returned mk_ini must be released with mk_ini_release when no longer needed.
Do not use the handle after it has been released.

functions.name: mk_ini_default
functions.signature: API_EXPORT mk_ini API_CALL mk_ini_default();
functions.description: Returns the global default INI configuration object. This is a shared instance intended for reading or as a base for configuration. Do not release it with mk_ini_release.
requirements: Do not call mk_ini_release on the returned global default object.

functions.name: mk_ini_load_string
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_ini_load_string(mk_ini ini, const char *str);
functions.description: Parses and loads INI configuration content from a null-terminated string into the specified ini object, replacing or augmenting its current state per the implementation.
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini created by mk_ini_create or obtained from mk_ini_default.
str must point to a valid null-terminated INI content string.

functions.name: mk_ini_load_file
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_ini_load_file(mk_ini ini, const char *file);
functions.description: Loads INI configuration from a file path into the specified ini object.
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini created by mk_ini_create or obtained from mk_ini_default.
file must be a valid, null-terminated file system path to an INI file that is readable by the process.

functions.name: mk_ini_release
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_ini_release(mk_ini ini);
functions.description: Destroys an INI configuration object created with mk_ini_create and releases its resources.
requirements: ini must be a mk_ini previously created by mk_ini_create.
Do not pass the global default ini returned by mk_ini_default to this function.
Do not use ini after it has been released.

functions.name: mk_ini_set_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_ini_set_option(mk_ini ini, const char *key, const char *value);
functions.description: Adds or updates a configuration option in the ini object. Keys use a two-part form like "field.key".
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini.
key must be a valid null-terminated string in two-part form like "field.key".
value must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: mk_ini_set_option_int
functions.signature: API_EXPORT void API_CALL mk_ini_set_option_int(mk_ini ini, const char *key, int value);
functions.description: Adds or updates an integer configuration option in the ini object using a two-part key like "field.key".
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini.
key must be a valid null-terminated string in two-part form like "field.key".

functions.name: mk_ini_get_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT const char *API_CALL mk_ini_get_option(mk_ini ini, const char *key);
functions.description: Retrieves the value of a configuration option. Returns NULL if the option does not exist. The returned pointer is owned by the ini object; do not free it.
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini.
key must be a valid null-terminated string in two-part form like "field.key".
Caller must handle a NULL return indicating the option is absent.
Do not free or modify the returned pointer; its lifetime is tied to ini.

functions.name: mk_ini_del_option
functions.signature: API_EXPORT int API_CALL mk_ini_del_option(mk_ini ini, const char *key);
functions.description: Deletes a configuration option. Returns 1 on success, 0 if the option did not exist.
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini.
key must be a valid null-terminated string in two-part form like "field.key".
Caller should check the return value: 1 indicates deletion succeeded; 0 indicates the key was not present.

functions.name: mk_ini_dump_string
functions.signature: API_EXPORT char *API_CALL mk_ini_dump_string(mk_ini ini);
functions.description: Exports the ini object to an INI-formatted string. The returned buffer is allocated by the mk API and must be freed with mk_free.
requirements: ini must be a valid mk_ini.
The returned pointer must be freed with mk_free when no longer needed.
Do not free the returned pointer with free or delete.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path
# This generator emits a bytes blob that the fuzzing runtime will split to feed
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR (as C strings) and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (as filenames that should
# point to existing, readable/writable data when needed).
#
# Strategy:
# - Encode multiple newline-separated records. The fuzzer runtime typically
#   reads sequential chunks; giving a catalog of plausible paths and strings
#   increases chances the stubs pick appropriate ones.
# - Include a mix of absolute and relative paths, Unix and Windows styles,
#   directories and files, with and without extensions, and with URL-like
#   components if used as general strings elsewhere.
# - Include paths that usually exist in most environments (like ".", "..",
#   temp-like names) and names that are safe to create or treat as files.
# - Keep total under 4096 bytes.

SEP = "\n"

def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _unix_rel_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts = []
    # Simple relatives
    parts += [
        ".",
        "..",
        "./",
        "../",
        "./" + _rand_alnum(rng, 6),
        "../" + _rand_alnum(rng, 6),
        "logs/app.log",
        "var/data.db",
        "tmp/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 8) + ".bin",
        "config/settings.ini",
        "media/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5) + ".mp4",
        "hls/index.m3u8",
        "hls/stream0.ts",
    ]
    # Nested
    n = rng.randint(2, 4)
    nested = "/".join(_rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(3, 7)) for _ in range(n))
    parts.append(nested)
    parts.append(nested + "/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5) + ".txt")
    return parts

def _unix_abs_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts = [
        "/tmp/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 6),
        "/var/tmp/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 6) + ".dat",
        "/var/log/zlm.log",
        "/etc/hosts",
        "/usr/local/share/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5),
        "/opt/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 4) + "/config.ini",
        "/home/user/" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5) + ".mp4",
    ]
    return parts

def _win_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    drive = rng.choice(list(string.ascii_uppercase)) + ":\\"
    parts = [
        drive + "Temp\\" + _rand_alnum(rng, 6) + ".tmp",
        drive + "logs\\zlm.log",
        drive + "Users\\Public\\Videos\\" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5) + ".mp4",
        "..\\" + _rand_alnum(rng, 5) + "\\config.ini",
        ".\\data\\" + _rand_alnum(rng, 4) + ".bin",
    ]
    return parts

def _urls(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Some APIs accept general strings; include URL-like strings which might be used as options
    host = _rand_alnum(rng, 6).lower()
    app = _rand_alnum(rng, 4).lower()
    stream = _rand_alnum(rng, 6).lower()
    q = f"token={_rand_alnum(rng,8)}&vhost=__defaultVhost__"
    return [
        f"http://{host}/index.html",
        f"https://{host}/file.txt",
        f"rtsp://{host}/{app}/{stream}",
        f"rtmp://{host}/{app}/{stream}",
        f"rtc://__defaultVhost__/{app}/{stream}?{q}",
    ]

def _ini_samples() -> List[str]:
    # Key strings that look like INI keys or contents
    return [
        "general.enableVhost=1",
        "http.port=80",
        "rtmp.port=1935",
        "rtsp.port=554",
        "ffmpeg.cmd=ffmpeg",
    ]

def _headers_like(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        "Content-Type", "text/plain",
        "Content-Type", "application/octet-stream",
        "Range", "bytes=0-1023",
        "User-Agent", "fuzz-agent/1.0",
    ]

def _ensure_existing_filenames(candidates: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    # We cannot perform I/O creation; but FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME ensures existence itself.
    # Still include common existing pseudo-paths like "." to increase chance of success for directory-based logic.
    return candidates + ["."]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    items: List[str] = []

    # Mix of paths and general strings
    items += _unix_rel_paths(rng)
    items += _unix_abs_paths(rng)
    items += _win_paths(rng)
    items += _urls(rng)
    items += _ini_samples()

    # Augment with a few random file-like names
    for _ in range(5):
        name = _rand_alnum(rng, rng.randint(4, 10))
        ext = rng.choice([".log", ".txt", ".ini", ".mp4", ".ts", ".m3u8", ".bin"]) 
        rel = name + ext
        items.append(rel)

    # Headers-like key/values as standalone strings
    items += _headers_like(rng)

    # Ensure some candidates that are trivially accessible
    items = _ensure_existing_filenames(items)

    # De-duplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    deduped = []
    for s in items:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            deduped.append(s)

    # Join with newlines; limit size to 4096 bytes
    payload = SEP.join(deduped)
    b = payload.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Trim from the end
        b = b[:4096]
        # Ensure we don't cut in middle of a multibyte sequence
        try:
            b = b.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore').encode('utf-8')
        except Exception:
            pass
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Data type: INI configuration text
# Goal: Produce valid, interesting INI content that covers:
# - multiple sections
# - keys with different value types (ints, bools, floats, strings)
# - repeated keys (last one wins)
# - keys without section (global)
# - comments (; and # styles)
# - whitespace variations and quoted strings
# - unicode and escapings
# - empty values
# - long lines and many keys but keep total <= 4096 bytes
# This feeds mk_ini_load_string(ini, str) which expects a null-terminated C string

BOOLS = ["0", "1", "true", "false", "on", "off", "yes", "no", "True", "False"]
SECTIONS = [
    "general", "http", "rtsp", "rtmp", "rtc", "log", "record", "hls", "mp4",
    "auth", "proxy", "pusher", "downloader", "decoder", "transcode"
]

# Some keys mirroring ZLMediaKit common options (not exhaustive, just plausible)
KEYS = [
    # global/runtime
    "system.thread_num", "system.log_level", "system.log_mask", "system.log_file_days",
    # http/rtsp/rtmp servers
    "http.port", "http.sslport", "http.keepalive_ms", "http.root",
    "rtsp.port", "rtsp.sslport", "rtmp.port", "rtmp.sslport",
    # player/pusher
    "player.protocol_timeout_ms", "player.media_timeout_ms", "player.wait_track_ready",
    "pusher.protocol_timeout_ms", "pusher.media_timeout_ms", "pusher.beat_interval_ms",
    # record
    "record.enable", "record.app", "record.max_second", "record.file_path",
    # hls/mp4
    "hls.enable", "hls.segment_ms", "hls.save_path", "mp4.enable", "mp4.max_second",
    # auth
    "auth.enable", "auth.user", "auth.passwd",
    # proxy
    "proxy.retry_count", "proxy.enable_hls", "proxy.enable_mp4",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "路径/录像", "测试", "用户", "密码", "пример", "δοκιμή", "測試", "テスト"
]

def rnd_ident(rnd: random.Random, min_len=5, max_len=12) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    l = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(letters) for _ in range(l))

def rnd_path(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = ["/var", "log", rnd_ident(rnd, 3, 8)]
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rnd.choice(["hls", "mp4", "rec", "zl"]))
    return "/" + "/".join(parts)

def rnd_string_val(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # mix ascii, spaces, quotes, and occasional unicode
    chunks: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            chunks.append(rnd.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        else:
            s = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.") for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 12)))
            chunks.append(s)
    val = " ".join(chunks)
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        # optionally quote and escape
        val = '"' + val.replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
    return val

def rnd_value_for_key(rnd: random.Random, key: str) -> str:
    # try to match plausible types for some keys
    k = key.lower()
    if any(x in k for x in ["port", "ms", "second", "timeout", "interval", "thread_num", "log_level", "log_mask", "days", "fps", "bit_rate", "retry_count"]):
        # integer range
        if "port" in k:
            return str(rnd.randint(0, 65535))
        if "log_level" in k:
            return str(rnd.randint(0, 4))
        if "days" in k:
            return str(rnd.randint(0, 30))
        return str(rnd.randint(0, 120000))
    if any(x in k for x in ["enable", "wait_track_ready"]):
        return rnd.choice(BOOLS)
    if any(x in k for x in ["path", "root", "file"]):
        # sometimes quoted path
        p = rnd_path(rnd)
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            p += "/" + rnd_ident(rnd, 4, 10) + rnd.choice([".mp4", ".m3u8", ".log"]) 
        if rnd.random() < 0.4:
            p = '"' + p + '"'
        return p
    if any(x in k for x in ["user", "passwd", "app", "vhost", "stream"]):
        return rnd_string_val(rnd)
    # default mixed types
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.3:
        return rnd.choice(BOOLS)
    if choice < 0.6:
        return str(rnd.randint(0, 10000))
    if choice < 0.8:
        return f"{rnd.uniform(0, 10):.3f}"
    return rnd_string_val(rnd)

def make_section(rnd: random.Random, name: str, kvs: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"[{name}]")
    # add a header comment sometimes
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"; auto-generated section {name}")
    for k, v in kvs:
        # introduce whitespace variations
        ws_left = "" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else " " * rnd.randint(0, 2)
        ws_right = "" if rnd.random() < 0.5 else " " * rnd.randint(0, 2)
        eq = "=" if rnd.random() < 0.8 else ":"
        line = f"{ws_left}{k}{ws_right}{eq}{ws_right}{v}"
        lines.append(line)
        # occasional inline comment
        if rnd.random() < 0.2:
            lines[-1] += f"  ; note {rnd_ident(rnd, 3, 6)}"
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def make_global_block(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    # comments at top
    lines.append("; ZLMediaKit INI example generated for fuzz seeding")
    lines.append("# Both ; and # comments should be supported by many INI parsers")
    lines.append("")
    # a couple of global keys (no section)
    globals_keys = ["system.thread_num", "system.log_level", "system.log_mask", "system.log_file_days"]
    for k in globals_keys:
        v = rnd_value_for_key(rnd, k)
        lines.append(f"{k} = {v}")
    # duplicate key to test override
    if rnd.random() < 0.9:
        k = rnd.choice(globals_keys)
        v = rnd_value_for_key(rnd, k)
        lines.append(f"{k} = {v}  ; override")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.append(make_global_block(rnd))

    # choose a subset of sections
    section_names = rnd.sample(SECTIONS, k=rnd.randint(5, min(9, len(SECTIONS))))

    # Build key-value pairs per section
    used_keys = set()
    for name in section_names:
        kvs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
        # include some generic keys by mapping KEYS into this section namespace, and a few random ones
        nkeys = rnd.randint(5, 14)
        for _ in range(nkeys):
            if rnd.random() < 0.7 and KEYS:
                base = rnd.choice(KEYS)
            else:
                base = f"{name}.{rnd_ident(rnd, 4, 10)}"
            # occasionally repeat keys to test last-one-wins
            key = base if rnd.random() < 0.8 else base
            # Ensure some variety across whole file
            if rnd.random() < 0.2:
                key = f"{name}.{rnd_ident(rnd, 4, 10)}"
            val = rnd_value_for_key(rnd, key)
            kvs.append((key, val))
            used_keys.add(key)
        # add intentional duplicate of one key within section
        if kvs and rnd.random() < 0.8:
            kdup, _ = rnd.choice(kvs)
            kvs.append((kdup, rnd_value_for_key(rnd, kdup)))
        parts.append(make_section(rnd, name, kvs))

    # trailing block with edge cases
    edge_lines: List[str] = []
    edge_lines.append("[edge]")
    # empty value
    edge_lines.append("empty_key=")
    # quoted with escapes
    edge_lines.append('quoted_key="value with spaces and \\"quotes\\" inside"')
    # boolean variants
    for b in BOOLS[:6]:
        edge_lines.append(f"flag_{b} = {b}")
    # very long value line but within limits
    long_val = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(512))
    edge_lines.append(f"long_value={long_val}")
    # unicode path
    edge_lines.append(f"unicode_path=/{rnd.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)}/{rnd.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)}")
    parts.append("\n".join(edge_lines))

    content = "\n".join(parts)

    # ensure total size <= 4096 bytes; if too large, trim by removing some sections safely
    if len(content.encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
        # Keep header and edge, trim middle
        head = parts[0]
        tail = parts[-1]
        middle = parts[1:-1]
        # progressively drop middle sections until under limit
        while middle and len((head + "\n" + "\n".join(middle) + "\n" + tail).encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
            middle.pop(rnd.randrange(len(middle)))
        content = head + "\n" + "\n".join(middle) + "\n" + tail

    # Final newline at end is typical for text files
    if not content.endswith("\n"):
        content += "\n"

    return content.encode('utf-8')

def make_ssl_inline_contents(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Inline PEM combo and dummy PFX bytes (for content mode)
    out: List[bytes] = []
    out.append(PEM_CERT)
    out.append(PEM_KEY)
    # Sometimes concatenate cert+key
    out.append(PEM_CERT + b"\n" + PEM_KEY)
    # Dummy PFX blob and with password hint in same buffer
    pwd = random_password(rng).encode('utf-8')
    out.append(PFX_HEADER + b"PWD:" + pwd)
    return out

def random_password(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789!@#$_-"
    n = rng.randrange(4, 16)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def pack_null_terminated(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Join chunks each terminated with \0, and end with an extra \0 to help parsers
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    size = 0
    for c in chunks:
        if size + len(c) + 1 > MAX_BUF:
            break
        parts.append(c + b"\x00")
        size += len(c) + 1
    # trailing sentinel
    if size + 1 <= MAX_BUF:
        parts.append(b"\x00")
    return b"".join(parts)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Log file candidates
    chunks.extend(make_logfile_paths(rng))

    # 2) INI paths and inline content
    chunks.extend(make_ini_path_variants(rng))

    # 3) SSL certificate paths
    chunks.extend(make_cert_path_variants(rng))

    # 4) SSL inline contents options (when ssl_is_path==0)
    chunks.extend(make_ssl_inline_contents(rng))

    # 5) SSL password candidates (empty, simple, complex)
    chunks.extend([
        b"",  # empty password
        b"password",
        random_password(rng).encode('utf-8'),
        b"123456",
        b"zlm-secret",
    ])

    # 6) Also provide a few generic directories that may be valid
    dirs = [
        b"/etc/ssl/\x00" if os.name != 'nt' else b"C:\\ProgramData\\ssl\x00",
        b"./certs/",
        b"../ssl/",
    ]
    chunks.extend(dirs)

    # Shuffle to diversify slicing positions between runs with same seed space
    rng.shuffle(chunks)

    return pack_null_terminated(chunks)[:MAX_BUF]

import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a password/passphrase string buffer.
# Target usage observed:
# - mk_rtsp_auth_invoker_do(ctx, encrypted, pwd_or_md5): when encrypted==0, expects plaintext password;
#   when encrypted!=0, expects MD5 hash string. Fuzzer stub toggles the encrypted flag randomly, so
#   we should sometimes return a plausible MD5 hex digest, and sometimes a plausible plaintext password.
# - mk_env_init/mk_env_init2: ssl_pwd may be used as a certificate/password; plaintext is expected.
# Therefore we produce a mix of:
#  - plaintext passwords with varied lengths/character classes
#  - 32-hex MD5 digests (lower/upper/mixed case) optionally with/without leading zeros
#  - edge but valid values like empty string or very long passphrases (kept <= 4096 bytes)
#  - common patterns (words + digits + symbols) to exercise parsers
# No I/O and deterministic via seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

COMMON_WORDS = [
    "admin", "root", "guest", "user", "password", "pass", "secret", "stream", "media",
    "rtsp", "rtmp", "webrtc", "ssl", "tls", "cert", "key", "zlm", "zlmediakit"
]
SYMBOLS = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}:;,.?/\\|~"
HEXLOW = "0123456789abcdef"
HEXUP = HEXLOW.upper()


def _rand_md5_hex(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a 32-char hex digest, sometimes upper, sometimes lower, sometimes mixed.
    chars = [rng.choice((HEXLOW, HEXUP)[rng.randrange(2)]) for _ in range(32)]
    # Occasionally mix cases within the string
    s = "".join(ch[rng.randrange(len(ch))] if isinstance(ch, str) else ch for ch in chars)
    # Optionally add a common MD5 presentation quirk (none actually, keep 32-hex strictly)
    return s


def _rand_plain_password(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose length with a biased distribution: short (4-8), medium (9-16), long (17-64), very long (65-1024)
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.25:
        length = rng.randint(4, 8)
    elif roll < 0.65:
        length = rng.randint(9, 16)
    elif roll < 0.95:
        length = rng.randint(17, 64)
    else:
        length = rng.randint(65, 1024)

    # Ensure presence of classes: lower, upper, digit, symbol, but not always (some systems allow any string)
    pools: List[str] = [string.ascii_lowercase, string.ascii_uppercase, string.digits, SYMBOLS]
    required = []
    # 70% chance to enforce each class
    for pool in pools:
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            required.append(rng.choice(pool))

    # Add some common words concatenated with digits/symbols
    parts: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts.append(rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 9999)))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(rng.choice(SYMBOLS))

    base = "".join(parts)
    # Fill remaining length with mixed characters
    allchars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + SYMBOLS
    remaining = max(0, length - len(base) - len(required))
    middle = "".join(rng.choice(allchars) for _ in range(remaining))
    pwd = base + middle + "".join(required)

    # Shuffle to avoid fixed pattern positions
    pwd_list = list(pwd)
    rng.shuffle(pwd_list)
    return "".join(pwd_list)


def _maybe_empty_or_simple(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes return very simple but valid strings, including empty.
    options = [
        "",  # empty string
        "0",
        "123456",
        "password",
        "letmein",
        "admin",
        "P@ssw0rd",
    ]
    return rng.choice(options)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide the kind of output to generate
    kind = rng.choices(
        population=["md5", "plain", "simple"],
        weights=[0.35, 0.55, 0.10],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if kind == "md5":
        s = _rand_md5_hex(rng)
    elif kind == "plain":
        s = _rand_plain_password(rng)
    else:
        s = _maybe_empty_or_simple(rng)

    # Constrain size and return as bytes (UTF-8). If longer than MAX_SIZE, truncate.
    if len(s) > MAX_SIZE:
        s = s[:MAX_SIZE]
    return s.encode("utf-8")

]

    s = ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))
    # Ensure it doesn't start/end with '.' accidentally
    return s.strip('.') or 'k'

def _make_dotted(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 60% choose known dotted, else compose field.key (and sometimes field.sub.key)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return _rand_choice(rng, KNOWN_DOTTED)
    field = _rand_choice(rng, KNOWN_FIELDS)
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # three-part
        return f"{field}.{_rand_token(rng)}.{_rand_choice(rng, KNOWN_KEYS)}"
    return f"{field}.{_rand_choice(rng, KNOWN_KEYS)}"

def _make_single(rng: random.Random) -> str:

            "protocol_timeout_ms", "media_timeout_ms", "beat_interval_ms",
            "wait_track_ready", "rtsp_speed", "file_max_size", "file_max_count",
        ])
    return _rand_token(rng, 1, 12)

def _make_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate plausible values: integers, booleans, small strings, paths
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.35:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 20000))
    if r < 0.55:
        return _rand_choice(rng, ["0", "1", "true", "false", "on", "off"])
    if r < 0.75:

        return _rand_token(rng, 1, 16)
    # path-like
    parts = [ _rand_token(rng, 1, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,3)) ]
    return "/" + "/".join(parts)

def _pack_cstrs(strs: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated strings
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strs:
        out.extend(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
        out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:

    # We keep under 4096 bytes.
    entries: List[str] = []

    # Mix of dotted keys for mk_ini_* and single keys for mk_set_option/mk_get_option
    count = rng.randint(4, 12)
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            key = _make_dotted(rng)

            key = _make_single(rng)

        entries.extend([key, val])

    entries.extend([
        "player.protocol_timeout_ms", "5000",
        "player.media_timeout_ms", "15000",
        "log.file_max_size", "10",
        "log.file_max_count", "5",
        "record.enable", "1",
        "pusher.rtp_type", "0",
        "proxy.rtp_type", "1",
    ])

    blob = _pack_cstrs(entries)
    # Ensure size cap
    return blob[:4096]

    lambda s: s,  # identity

]

def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:

    return "".join(rng.choice(TOKEN_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]


def _maybe_case_variant(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    fn = rng.choice(CASE_VARIANTS)
    return fn(s)


def _generate_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Strategy mix:
    #  - 40%: common headers
    #  - 30%: common query keys
    #  - 20%: random token
    #  - 10%: composite tokens (prefix.suffix or X-Custom-*)
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.4:
        base = _weighted_choice(rng, COMMON_HEADER_KEYS)
        return _maybe_case_variant(rng, base)
    elif roll < 0.7:
        base = _weighted_choice(rng, COMMON_QUERY_KEYS)
        return _maybe_case_variant(rng, base)
    elif roll < 0.9:
        return _rand_token(rng)
    else:
        # Composite forms
        style = rng.randrange(3)
        if style == 0:
            # dotted option (ini-like)
            return f"{_rand_token(rng,1,8)}.{_rand_token(rng,1,12)}"
        elif style == 1:
            # X-Custom-*
            return "X-" + _rand_token(rng, 3, 10) + ("-" + _rand_token(rng, 2, 8) if rng.random() < 0.5 else "")
        else:
            # underscore separated
            return _rand_token(rng, 2, 8) + "_" + _rand_token(rng, 2, 12)

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create between 1 and 4 keys concatenated by nulls to allow multiple reads
    # by a harness that may consume more than one FUZZ_PARAM_STR from the same buffer.
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    keys = []
    total_len = 0
    for _ in range(count):
        k = _generate_key(rng)
        # Ensure non-empty and ASCII-safe
        if not k:
            k = "k"
        keys.append(k)
        total_len += len(k) + 1  # include NUL separator
        if total_len > 4000:
            break
    # Join with NUL separators and ensure final NUL termination
    blob = ("\0".join(keys) + "\0").encode("ascii", errors="ignore")
    # Cap to 4096 bytes
    return blob[:4096]

import random
from typing import List

# Max output size per requirements
MAX_OUT = 4096

# Helpers

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

# H.264 Annex-B NAL builder
# nalu_type: 1=non-IDR, 5=IDR, 7=SPS, 8=PPS, 9=AUD

def _h264_nal(rng: random.Random, nalu_type: int, payload_len: int) -> bytes:
    start = b"\x00\x00\x01" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"\x00\x00\x00\x01"
    nal_header = (((rng.randint(0, 3) & 0x3) << 5) | (nalu_type & 0x1F)).to_bytes(1, 'big')
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, payload_len))
    return start + nal_header + payload

# H.265 Annex-B NAL builder (approximate header layout)

def _h265_nal(rng: random.Random, nalu_type: int, payload_len: int) -> bytes:
    start = b"\x00\x00\x01" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"\x00\x00\x00\x01"
    b0 = ((nalu_type & 0x3F) << 1) | (rng.getrandbits(1))
    b1 = rng.getrandbits(8)
    hdr = bytes((b0, b1))
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, max(0, payload_len))
    return start + hdr + payload

# Minimal GOP-like sequences

def _h264_gop(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    sps = _h264_nal(rng, 7, rng.randint(8, 32))
    pps = _h264_nal(rng, 8, rng.randint(6, 24))
    aud = _h264_nal(rng, 9, rng.randint(2, 8))
    idr = _h264_nal(rng, 5, rng.randint(50, 300))
    p1 = _h264_nal(rng, 1, rng.randint(20, 120))
    return aud + sps + pps + idr + p1

def _h265_gop(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    vps = _h265_nal(rng, 32, rng.randint(8, 24))
    sps = _h265_nal(rng, 33, rng.randint(8, 32))
    pps = _h265_nal(rng, 34, rng.randint(6, 24))
    aud = _h265_nal(rng, 35, rng.randint(2, 8))
    idr = _h265_nal(rng, 19, rng.randint(60, 320))
    return aud + vps + sps + pps + idr

# HTTP-like text payload

def _http_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    methods = [b"GET", b"POST", b"PUT", b"DELETE"]
    path_choices = [b"/", b"/index.html", b"/api", b"/upload"]
    headers = [
        b"Host: example.com",
        b"User-Agent: fuzz/1.0",
        b"Content-Type: application/octet-stream",
        b"Accept: */*",
        b"Connection: keep-alive",
    ]
    m = rng.choice(methods)
    p = rng.choice(path_choices)
    body = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 128))
    hdr = b"\r\n".join(rng.sample(headers, rng.randint(2, len(headers))))
    req = m + b" " + p + b" HTTP/1.1\r\n" + hdr + b"\r\n\r\n" + body
    return req

# Random binary block with sprinkled zeros/0xFF; safe for sz==0

def _binary_block(rng: random.Random, sz: int) -> bytes:
    if sz <= 0:
        return b""
    data = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, sz))
    sprinkle = max(1, sz // 16)
    for _ in range(sprinkle):
        idx = rng.randrange(sz)
        data[idx] = 0
    for _ in range(sprinkle):
        idx = rng.randrange(sz)
        data[idx] = 0xFF
    return bytes(data)

# Edge-case small buffers

def _edge_small_buffers(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        b"",            # zero-length for hex-dump callers
        b"x",           # minimal one byte
        b"\x00",        # single NUL
        b"A" * rng.randint(2, 16),
    ]

# Compose combined payload with mixed content

def _compose_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        chunks.append(_h264_gop(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(_h265_gop(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        chunks.append(_http_like(rng))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.append(_binary_block(rng, rng.randint(16, 256)))
    chunks.extend(_edge_small_buffers(rng))

    delim = b"\r\n--FUZZ--\r\n"
    out = b""
    for i, c in enumerate(chunks):
        if not c and rng.random() < 0.5:
            continue
        out += c
        if i != len(chunks) - 1 and rng.random() < 0.7:
            out += delim
        if len(out) >= MAX_OUT:
            break

    if len(out) > MAX_OUT:
        out = out[:MAX_OUT]
    if len(out) == 0:
        out = b"z"
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.2:
        buf = _h264_gop(rng)
    elif mode < 0.35:
        buf = _h265_gop(rng)
    elif mode < 0.5:
        # HTTP-like plus optional binary tail; allow 0-size tail safely
        tail = _binary_block(rng, rng.randint(0, 128))
        buf = _http_like(rng) + tail
    else:
        buf = _compose_payload(rng)

    if len(buf) > MAX_OUT:
        buf = buf[:MAX_OUT]
    if len(buf) == 0:
        buf = b"x"
    return buf

# Data type: hostname or IP
# We need to generate bytes that fuzzer will use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FILENAMES.
# Target stubs want:
# - mk_media_source_start_send_rtp*: dst (destination URL/host), ssrc (string), con_type range handled by stub
# - mk_media_start_send_rtp*: url must be non-empty and scheme-valid (rtsp/rtmp handled by stub building), ssrc decimal
